3. Read the Installment No column top to bottom and confirm the numbers increase one by one starting from the first installment.
4. Confirm there is no gap in the sequence and no number repeats for a different scheduled installment.
5. Confirm the installment number on each row matches the number shown for the same installment on the plan window.
6. Re-sort by transaction date and confirm the installment numbers stay attached to their own rows.

Description: [New] A failed attempt and its retry share the same installment number, so the sequence is not broken
Pre-requisite Data: Plan1 = plan whose installment N1 failed once and was retried successfully; Txn-F = the failed attempt; Txn-R = the successful retry.
Test Data: Filter Payment Transaction Tracking to Plan1 and inspect the installment numbers of Txn-F and Txn-R.
Expected Output: Both the failed attempt and the retry carry installment number N1; the retry does not consume a new number, so the sequence of installments stays unbroken.
Verification Step:
1. Open Payment Transaction Tracking and filter to Plan1.
2. Locate Txn-F and Txn-R for the same installment.
3. Confirm both rows show the same Installment No, N1.
4. Confirm the next scheduled installment still carries N1 + 1 and was not pushed forward by the retry.
5. Confirm reading the whole list still gives a gap-free sequence.
6. Confirm the plan window shows the same installment number for that installment.

Description: [New] Several consecutive Pay Now payments each take the next installment number (last + 1 each time)
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with active plan Plan1 whose highest existing installment number is N1; PayNow1, PayNow2, PayNow3 = three Pay Now payments collected one after another on Plan1.
Test Data: Collect PayNow1, then PayNow2, then PayNow3 on Plan1 and read the Installment No of each resulting transaction.
Expected Output: The first Pay Now is numbered N1 + 1, the second N1 + 2 and the third N1 + 3 — each Pay Now takes the next number after the highest one existing at that moment, with no duplicates.
Verification Step:
1. Open Plan1 and note the highest installment number N1.
2. Collect PayNow1 successfully and confirm in Payment Transaction Tracking that its Installment No is N1 + 1.
3. Collect PayNow2 successfully and confirm its Installment No is N1 + 2.
4. Collect PayNow3 successfully and confirm its Installment No is N1 + 3.
5. Confirm no two of the three rows share an installment number.
6. Confirm the originally scheduled installments keep their own numbers unchanged.
7. Reopen the screen and confirm the numbers persist as recorded.

Description: [New] Pay Now on a plan that has no installment recorded yet gets the first installment number
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with a newly created plan Plan-New on which no installment has been processed and no installment row exists yet; PayNow1 = the first Pay Now payment collected on Plan-New.
Test Data: Collect PayNow1 on Plan-New before any scheduled charge has run, then open Payment Transaction Tracking.
Expected Output: With no previous installment to count from, the Pay Now transaction is numbered as the first installment (1) rather than showing blank, zero or an error.
Verification Step:
1. Open Plan-New and confirm no installment has been processed yet.
2. Collect PayNow1 through Pay Now and complete it successfully.
3. Open Payment Transaction Tracking and locate the PayNow1 transaction.
4. Confirm its Installment No is 1 and is neither blank nor zero nor a negative value.
5. Confirm no error or warning was raised while creating the transaction.
6. Let the first scheduled charge run afterwards and confirm it continues the sequence rather than reusing number 1.

Description: [New] A Pay Now transaction keeps its place in the sequential installment ordering of the plan
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with plan Plan1 having scheduled installments up to N1 plus one Pay Now transaction numbered N1 + 1.
Test Data: Filter Payment Transaction Tracking to Plan1, sort by Installment No and inspect the ordering.
Expected Output: The Pay Now row sits at the end of the sequence as N1 + 1 and the scheduled installments keep their original order, so the whole list still reads as one continuous sequence.
Verification Step:
1. Open Payment Transaction Tracking and filter to Plan1.
2. Sort the list by Installment No ascending.
3. Confirm the scheduled installments appear in their original order from the first number to N1.
4. Confirm the Pay Now row appears immediately after them as N1 + 1.
5. Confirm no scheduled installment was renumbered to make room for the Pay Now row.
6. Confirm the plan window shows the same sequence for the same transactions.

Description: [New] Filtering by In queue and by In progress returns the same rows (round-trip of the mapped status)
Pre-requisite Data: Txn-Q = a plan charge queued for processing; Txn-IP = an older transaction stored with the In progress status; Txn-S = a successful transaction used as a control.
Test Data: Apply the Transaction Status filter as In queue, then as In progress, and compare the two result sets.
Expected Output: Because In queue is mapped to the existing In progress status, both filter values return exactly the same rows, and neither returns successful or failed transactions.
Verification Step:
1. Open Payment Transaction Tracking and set Transaction Status = In queue; note every row returned.
2. Clear the filter and set Transaction Status = In progress.
3. Confirm exactly the same rows are returned, including both Txn-Q and Txn-IP.
4. Confirm Txn-S is excluded from both result sets.
5. Confirm the row count and the totals are identical for both filter values.
6. Combine the status filter with a plan-code filter and confirm the two status values still behave identically.
7. Clear the filter and confirm all rows return.

Description: [New] In queue and In progress rows are shown with the same status colour and are never counted as paid
Pre-requisite Data: Txn-Q = a queued plan charge; Txn-IP = an older In progress transaction; Txn-S = a successful transaction; Txn-F = a failed transaction.
Test Data: List Txn-Q, Txn-IP, Txn-S and Txn-F together and compare their status colouring and their effect on the totals.
Expected Output: Txn-Q and Txn-IP use the same pending colour as each other and a different colour from successful and failed rows; neither adds to collected totals.
Verification Step:
1. Open Payment Transaction Tracking so all four transactions are visible.
2. Confirm Txn-Q and Txn-IP carry the same pending status colour.
3. Confirm that colour is clearly different from the successful colour on Txn-S and the failed colour on Txn-F.
4. Confirm the status text on both pending rows describes the same pending state.
5. Confirm the collected/received totals include Txn-S but not Txn-Q or Txn-IP.
6. Re-sort the grid and confirm the colouring stays with the correct rows.

Description: [New] A full refund of a plan charge is never displayed at the payment-plan level
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with plan Plan1; Txn-S = a successful charge of Plan1 covering installment N1; Refund-Full = a full refund of Txn-S raised from Payment Transaction Tracking.
Test Data: Raise Refund-Full against Txn-S, then open the payment plan window of Plan1 and look for any refund information.
Expected Output: The plan window shows no refund row, no refund column, no refund amount and no refund icon — the refund only exists in Payment Transaction Tracking.
Verification Step:
1. Open Payment Transaction Tracking, select Txn-S and complete Refund-Full.
2. Confirm the refund is recorded and visible in Payment Transaction Tracking.
3. Open Plan1 for Pat1 and review the installment section and the plan summary.
4. Confirm no refund entry, refund column or refund total is displayed anywhere on the plan.
5. Confirm installment N1 keeps the status it already had and does not flip to a refunded state.
6. Refresh the plan window and confirm the refund still does not appear.
7. Confirm the refund remains fully visible on the transaction tracking screen.

Description: [New] A partial refund of a plan charge shows no partial-refund indicator at the payment-plan level
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with plan Plan1; Txn-S = a successful charge of Plan1; Refund-Part = a refund of only part of Txn-S's amount.
Test Data: Raise Refund-Part against Txn-S, then inspect the plan window of Plan1 for any partial-refund marking.
Expected Output: No partial-refund indicator, badge, amount or changed status appears on the plan level; the partial refund is visible only in Payment Transaction Tracking with the refunded amount.
Verification Step:
1. Open Payment Transaction Tracking, select Txn-S and raise Refund-Part for part of the amount.
2. Confirm the partial refund is recorded in Payment Transaction Tracking with the refunded portion.
3. Open Plan1 and review the installment row that Txn-S paid.
4. Confirm no partial-refund badge, icon, note or amount is shown for it.
5. Confirm the installment's paid amount and status on the plan are unchanged by the partial refund.
6. Confirm the plan balance shown on the plan window is not adjusted by the partial refund.
7. Reopen both screens and confirm the behaviour is consistent.

Description: [New] A partially applied plan credit is returned by the Unapplied filter
Pre-requisite Data: Credit-P = a payment-plan credit where part of the money has been applied to bills and part is still open; Credit-A = a plan credit that is fully applied.
Test Data: Apply the Unapplied filter on Payment Transaction Tracking and look for Credit-P and Credit-A.
Expected Output: Credit-P is listed because it still has an open portion, while Credit-A is excluded; the Unapplied column shows only the remaining open amount of Credit-P.
Verification Step:
1. Open Payment Transaction Tracking with no filters and confirm both Credit-P and Credit-A are present.
2. Apply the Unapplied filter.
3. Confirm Credit-P is still listed.
4. Confirm Credit-A is excluded from the result.
5. Confirm the Unapplied column of Credit-P shows only the still-open portion and not the whole collected amount.
6. Apply the rest of Credit-P to bills, re-apply the filter and confirm it now drops out as well.

Description: [New] The Unapplied filter returns a mixed set of plan credits and other open credits together
Pre-requisite Data: Credit-PP = a partially applied payment-plan credit; Credit-PU = a fully unapplied payment-plan credit; Credit-OP = a partially applied open credit created outside any plan; Credit-OU = a fully unapplied open credit created outside any plan.
Test Data: Apply the Unapplied filter and review the mixed result set of plan and non-plan credits.
Expected Output: All four credits are listed together under the Unapplied filter regardless of their source and regardless of whether they are partly or fully unapplied, so staff see every open credit in one place.
Verification Step:
1. Open Payment Transaction Tracking and apply the Unapplied filter.
2. Confirm Credit-PP and Credit-PU (plan credits) are both listed.
3. Confirm Credit-OP and Credit-OU (non-plan open credits) are also listed in the same grid.
4. Confirm each row's Unapplied column shows its own remaining open amount.
5. Confirm plan rows carry the plan columns while non-plan rows leave them blank.
6. Confirm the grand total of the Unapplied column equals the sum of the four remaining open amounts.
7. Clear the filter and confirm fully applied credits reappear in the list.

Description: [New] The Unapplied filter excludes credits that have been fully applied
Pre-requisite Data: Credit-A1 = a plan credit fully applied to bills; Credit-A2 = a non-plan open credit fully applied to bills; Credit-U = a credit with an open portion, used as a control.
Test Data: Apply the Unapplied filter and confirm the fully applied credits are not returned.
Expected Output: Neither Credit-A1 nor Credit-A2 is returned by the Unapplied filter, while Credit-U is; clearing the filter brings all three back.
Verification Step:
1. Open Payment Transaction Tracking without filters and confirm all three credits are listed.
2. Apply the Unapplied filter.
3. Confirm Credit-A1 is not returned.
4. Confirm Credit-A2 is not returned.
5. Confirm Credit-U is returned.
6. Confirm the grand total under the filter counts only the open amount of Credit-U.
7. Clear the filter and confirm all three credits are listed again.

Description: [New] A card-expiry failure shows a Failed transaction here while the plan shows the installment as Overdue
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with plan Plan1 on saved card Card-Exp whose expiry month has already passed; N1 = the installment whose scheduled charge is attempted on Card-Exp.
Test Data: Let the scheduled charge for installment N1 run against the expired card Card-Exp, then compare Payment Transaction Tracking and the plan window.
Expected Output: Payment Transaction Tracking records a Failed credit-card transaction for N1, and the plan window shows installment N1 with an Overdue status in its payment column.
Verification Step:
1. Confirm Plan1 uses Card-Exp and that its expiry has passed.
2. Let the scheduled charge for installment N1 run.
3. Open Payment Transaction Tracking and confirm a transaction exists for N1 with the Failed status and the failed colour.
4. Confirm no receipt or open credit was created for that failed transaction.
5. Open Plan1 and confirm installment N1 shows Overdue in the payment column.
6. Confirm the plan moved on to the next installment without marking N1 as paid.
7. Confirm the failure reason recorded on the transaction points to the card expiry.

Description: [New] A declined card shows a Failed transaction here while the plan installment becomes Overdue
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with plan Plan1 on a valid but declinable card Card-D (for example insufficient funds); N1 = the installment charged on Card-D.
Test Data: Let the scheduled charge for installment N1 be declined by the gateway, then compare both screens.
Expected Output: The declined attempt is recorded here as a Failed transaction with the decline reason, and installment N1 is shown as Overdue on the plan.
Verification Step:
1. Let the scheduled charge for installment N1 run and be declined.
2. Open Payment Transaction Tracking and confirm a Failed transaction exists for N1.
3. Confirm the status history or request content records the decline reason.
4. Confirm no receipt or open credit was produced for the declined attempt.
5. Open Plan1 and confirm installment N1 shows Overdue.
6. Confirm the Overdue amount at plan level includes this installment's amount.
7. Confirm no notification of successful payment was produced for it.

Description: [New] A without-gateway plan shows a Failed status here for the missed charge while the installment turns Overdue
Pre-requisite Data: Plan-WG = an active payment plan created with the Without Gateway option, so no automatic gateway charge takes place; N1 = the installment whose scheduled date has passed without payment.
Test Data: Let the scheduled date of installment N1 on Plan-WG pass without any manual payment, then review both screens.
Expected Output: The plan shows installment N1 as Overdue in the payment column; the transaction tracking screen shows the failed credit-card status for the missed charge rather than a successful one.
Verification Step:
1. Confirm Plan-WG is created with the Without Gateway option.
2. Let the scheduled date of installment N1 pass with no manual payment collected.
3. Open Plan-WG and confirm installment N1 shows Overdue in the payment column.
4. Open Payment Transaction Tracking and confirm the missed charge is not reported as successful.
5. Confirm no receipt or open credit was created automatically for N1.
6. Confirm the plan has moved on to the next installment while N1 stays Overdue.
7. Confirm the plan's Overdue Amount now includes N1's amount.

Description: [New] Surcharge-related columns are hidden in the Payment Transaction Tracking grid (surcharge deferred to a separate ER)
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with plan Plan1 having processed transactions; Col-Visible = the currently visible column list of the transaction tracking grid.
Test Data: Open Payment Transaction Tracking, review the header row and any column-chooser list for surcharge columns.
Expected Output: No surcharge column is visible in the grid; the amount columns are complete and correctly aligned without it, because surcharge handling is deferred to a separate ER.
Verification Step:
1. Open Payment Transaction Tracking with no filters.
2. Read the header row and confirm no surcharge column is displayed.
3. Open the column chooser (if available) and confirm no surcharge column can be switched on from the screen.
4. Confirm the remaining amount columns (amount, applied, unapplied, total) line up with their values and none is blank because of the removal.
5. Confirm the grand-total row totals only the visible amount columns.
6. Open the screen from a payment plan as well and confirm no surcharge column appears there either.

Description: [New] Surcharge-related columns are also absent from the Payment Transaction Tracking export
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with plan Plan1 having processed transactions; Export1 = the file produced by the export action of the transaction tracking screen.
Test Data: Export the transaction tracking list and inspect the header row of Export1.
Expected Output: The exported file carries the same columns as the screen and contains no surcharge column or surcharge values.
Verification Step:
1. Open Payment Transaction Tracking and note the visible columns.
2. Run the export action to produce Export1.
3. Open Export1 and read its header row.
4. Confirm no surcharge column is present in the export.
5. Confirm the export headers match the on-screen columns one for one and in the same order.
6. Confirm each exported row's values sit under the correct header with no shift caused by the removed column.
7. Export again after applying a filter and confirm the header set is unchanged.

Description: [New] A Without Gateway plan creates no transaction and no receipt automatically, so nothing is listed here
Pre-requisite Data: Pat-WG = patient with a newly created plan Plan-WG saved with the Without Gateway option and with no manual payment taken yet.
Test Data: Create and activate Plan-WG, let its first scheduled date arrive, then search Payment Transaction Tracking for Pat-WG.
Expected Output: No transaction row and no receipt is created automatically for Plan-WG, so the transaction tracking screen shows nothing for that plan until a manual payment is made.
Verification Step:
1. Create and activate Plan-WG for Pat-WG with the Without Gateway option.
2. Let the first scheduled date arrive without collecting anything manually.
3. Open Payment Transaction Tracking and search for Pat-WG or for Plan-WG's plan code.
4. Confirm no transaction row exists for Plan-WG.
5. Confirm no receipt or open credit has been produced for it on the receipt screens.
6. Confirm the empty result is presented cleanly with no error.
7. Confirm the plan itself still exists and is active on the plan screen.

Description: [New] A manual Pay Now on a Without Gateway plan creates the first transaction visible in this screen
Pre-requisite Data: Pat-WG = patient with active plan Plan-WG created with the Without Gateway option and with no transaction so far; PayNow-WG = a manual payment collected on Plan-WG through Pay Now.
Test Data: Collect PayNow-WG manually on Plan-WG and then open Payment Transaction Tracking.
Expected Output: Only after the manual Pay Now does a transaction appear for Plan-WG, showing the collected amount, its installment number and its receipt; before that the screen had nothing for this plan.
Verification Step:
1. Confirm Payment Transaction Tracking currently lists nothing for Plan-WG.
2. Open Plan-WG and collect PayNow-WG through the Pay Now option.
3. Complete the payment and confirm the receipt is shown to the user.
4. Open Payment Transaction Tracking and confirm exactly one new row now exists for Plan-WG.
5. Confirm the row shows the collected amount and the installment number given to the Pay Now payment.
6. Confirm the corresponding installment status on the plan updates from Overdue/Pending to Paid.
7. Confirm no extra automatic transaction was created alongside the manual one.

Description: [New] End-to-end: failed charge becomes Overdue on the plan and is cleared by a Pay Now, with both rows visible here
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with active plan Plan1; N1 = the installment whose scheduled charge fails; PayNow1 = the Pay Now payment later collected to clear the overdue amount.
Test Data: Fail the scheduled charge for N1, then collect PayNow1 for the overdue amount and review both screens.
Expected Output: The failed attempt and the later successful Pay Now both remain listed in Payment Transaction Tracking, and the installment on the plan moves from Overdue to Paid once the Pay Now succeeds.
Verification Step:
1. Let the scheduled charge for installment N1 fail and confirm the failed row appears in Payment Transaction Tracking.
2. Open Plan1 and confirm installment N1 shows Overdue and is included in the plan's Overdue Amount.
3. Collect PayNow1 for the overdue amount through Pay Now and complete it successfully.
4. Return to Payment Transaction Tracking and confirm both the earlier failed row and the new successful row are listed.
5. Confirm the successful row carries a receipt/open-credit number and the failed row does not.
6. Open Plan1 and confirm installment N1 now shows Paid and the Overdue Amount has reduced accordingly.
7. Confirm no duplicate payment was taken for the same installment.

Description: Two panes (Notification / Reminder) each with an Event Type (Appointment / Payment Plan)
Pre-requisite Data: User1 = user allowed to open the Notification/Reminder Preference screen; Clinic1 = clinic with both appointment and payment-plan features switched on.
Test Data: Event Type values Appointment, Payment Plan.
Expected Output: Both panes render; Event Type offers Appointment and Payment Plan; choosing Payment Plan reveals its events.
Verification Step:
1. Log in as User1 and open the Notification and Reminder Preference screen for Clinic1.
2. Confirm the screen shows two separate panes, one for Notification and one for Reminder.
3. Confirm each pane has its own Event Type selector.
4. Open the Event Type list in the Notification pane and confirm it offers Appointment and Payment Plan.
5. Select Payment Plan and confirm the Event list refreshes to the payment-plan events.
6. Repeat steps 4 and 5 in the Reminder pane and confirm the same two event types are offered.
7. Confirm choosing one pane's event type does not change the other pane's selection.
Test Case Relevance: Prefs - two panes + event type (WebIMS doc p2)

Description: Payment-Plan notification events: Payment successful, Payment failed, Payment Plan setup, Payment plan status change
Pre-requisite Data: User1 = user with access to the preference screen; the payment-plan notification events are configured in the system.
Test Data: Notification pane, Event Type = Payment Plan.
Expected Output: The event dropdown lists exactly those four notification events.
Verification Step:
1. Open the Notification pane of the preference screen.
2. Set Event Type = Payment Plan.
3. Open the Event dropdown.
4. Confirm it lists Payment successful, Payment failed, Payment Plan setup and Payment plan status change.
5. Confirm no reminder-only events (such as Payment Due or Card expiry) appear in this notification list.
6. Confirm no appointment events remain in the list once Payment Plan is selected.

Description: Payment-Plan reminder events: Payment Due, Card expiry
Pre-requisite Data: User1 = user with access to the preference screen; payment-plan reminder events are configured in the system.
Test Data: Reminder pane, Event Type = Payment Plan.
Expected Output: The event dropdown lists exactly Payment Due and Card expiry.
Verification Step:
1. Open the Reminder pane of the preference screen.
2. Set Event Type = Payment Plan.
3. Open the Event dropdown.
4. Confirm it lists Payment Due and Card expiry.
5. Confirm no notification-only events (such as Payment successful or Payment failed) appear here.
6. Switch Event Type to Appointment and confirm the appointment reminder events replace them.
Status Comment: Not required

Description: Notification row fields: Active, Event Type, Event*, Mode* (All/Call/Email/Text), Template*
Pre-requisite Data: Row-N = a notification preference row being created with Event Type = Payment Plan and Event = Payment failed; Template1 = an available letter template for that event.
Test Data: A Payment-failed notification row.
Expected Output: Each row exposes Active, Event Type, Event, Mode and Template; Event/Mode/Template required.
Verification Step:
1. Open the Notification pane and add Row-N.
2. Confirm the row exposes the fields Active, Event Type, Event, Mode and Template.
3. Confirm Event, Mode and Template are marked as mandatory.
4. Open the Mode list and confirm it offers All, Call, Email and Text.
5. Leave Event blank and try to save; confirm saving is blocked with a clear message.
6. Leave Mode blank and try to save; confirm saving is blocked.
7. Leave Template blank and try to save; confirm saving is blocked.
8. Fill Event, Mode and Template1 and confirm the row saves successfully.

Description: Reminder row fields incl. To Be Sent (After/Before/Immediate + value + unit) and Template
Pre-requisite Data: Row-R1 = a reminder row for Event = Payment Due; Row-R2 = a reminder row for Event = Card expiry; Template1 = an available letter template.
Test Data: Payment Due = Before 3 Days; Card expiry = Before 14 Days.
Expected Output: Each row exposes Active, Event Type, Event, Mode, To Be Sent and Template; Immediate hides value/unit.
Verification Step:
1. Open the Reminder pane and add Row-R1.
2. Confirm the row exposes Active, Event Type, Event, Mode, To Be Sent and Template.
3. Confirm the To Be Sent control offers After, Before and Immediate together with a numeric value and a unit.
4. Set To Be Sent = Before with a value and a unit and confirm both inputs accept the entry.
5. Change To Be Sent to Immediate and confirm the value and unit inputs are hidden or cleared.
6. Add Row-R2 for Card expiry and confirm it offers the same set of fields independently of Row-R1.
7. Save both rows and reopen the screen; confirm each row retained its own To Be Sent setting and Template1.

Description: Duplicate reminder setup is not allowed (Active + Event Type + Event + Mode)
Pre-requisite Data: Row-A = an already saved reminder row with a given Active flag, Event Type, Event and Mode; Row-B = a new reminder row entered with exactly the same four values.
Test Data: Add a second reminder row with the same Active + Event Type + Event + Mode as an existing one.
Expected Output: The duplicate is blocked; a reminder with the same active/event-type/event/mode combination cannot be created twice.
Verification Step:
1. Open the Reminder pane and confirm Row-A exists and is saved.
2. Add Row-B with the same Active flag, Event Type, Event and Mode as Row-A.
3. Try to save.
4. Confirm the save is blocked and a duplicate message identifies the clash.
5. Change only the Mode on Row-B and confirm it now saves successfully.
6. Confirm the original Row-A is untouched after the blocked attempt.
7. Reopen the screen and confirm only one row exists per Active + Event Type + Event + Mode combination.
Test Case Relevance: Prefs - no duplicate reminder (WebIMS doc p8)

Description: Immediate reminder is restricted when Event Type = Payment Plan
Pre-requisite Data: Row-PP = a reminder row in the Reminder pane with Event Type = Payment Plan; Row-APP = a reminder row with Event Type = Appointment.
Test Data: On a Payment-Plan reminder row set To Be Sent = Immediate.
Expected Output: Immediate is not allowed/blocked for Payment Plan reminders (only After/Before).
Verification Step:
1. Open the Reminder pane and set Event Type = Payment Plan on Row-PP.
2. Open the To Be Sent option list.
3. Confirm Immediate is either absent or shown greyed out and cannot be chosen.
4. Confirm After and Before are still selectable with a value and unit.
5. Attempt to save the row with Immediate forced in (if selectable) and confirm the save is blocked with a message.
6. On Row-APP set Event Type = Appointment and confirm Immediate is available there, proving the restriction is limited to Payment Plan.
Test Case Relevance: Prefs - immediate restricted for PP (WebIMS doc p9)
Status Comment: Need to be discussed

Description: Card-expiry reminder treats the last day of the month as the expiry date
Pre-requisite Data: Card1 = a saved card whose expiry is captured as a month and year only (no day); Lead1 = the lead time set on the Card expiry reminder; Exp-Last = the last calendar day of Card1's expiry month.
Test Data: Card exp 08/26 (only month/year stored); Card-expiry reminder Before 14 days.
Expected Output: The expiry date used for the reminder is the last day of the month (e.g. 08/31/26), and the reminder fires the configured lead time before it.
Verification Step:
1. Open the Reminder pane and configure the Card expiry reminder with lead time Lead1.
2. Attach Card1 to a patient payment plan.
3. Confirm the system treats Card1's expiry date as Exp-Last, the last day of its expiry month.
4. Move the business date (or wait) to Exp-Last minus Lead1 and run the reminder job.
5. Confirm the card-expiry reminder is sent on that date and not on the first day of the expiry month.
6. Confirm the reminder content refers to the expiry month/year of Card1 and prompts the patient to update the card.
7. Confirm no reminder was sent earlier or later than the configured lead time.
Test Case Relevance: Prefs - card expiry last-day (WebIMS doc p10)

Description: Notification/reminder emails use the clinic’s email setup as sender
Pre-requisite Data: Clinic1 = clinic with a configured outgoing email setup Email1; Pat1 = patient with an active plan and a valid email address; Event1 = any payment-plan notification configured with Mode that includes Email.
Test Data: Trigger a payment-plan email notification.
Expected Output: The email is sent using the clinic’s configured email setup as the sender.
Verification Step:
1. Confirm Clinic1's email setup Email1 is configured and active.
2. Configure Event1 with Email included in its Mode.
3. Trigger Event1 for Pat1.
4. Open the email received by Pat1 (or the outgoing mail log).
5. Confirm the sender address is the one configured in Email1 for Clinic1.
6. Confirm no generic, system or personal user address is used as sender.
7. Repeat for a reminder event and confirm the same clinic sender is used.
Test Case Relevance: Prefs - clinic email sender (WebIMS doc p10)

Description: Scopes: Patient Chart (per patient) and General (clinic default); Patient Chart now includes the Notification pane
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = any patient chart; Scope-G = the General (clinic default) preference scope; Scope-P = the Patient Chart preference scope of Pat1.
Test Data: Open scope = General, then Patient Chart (PAT204).
Expected Output: Both scopes exist; the Patient-Chart scope now shows the Notification pane as well as the Reminder pane (previously reminder-only).
Verification Step:
1. Open the preference screen in Scope-G.
2. Confirm both the Notification pane and the Reminder pane are available there.
3. Open the preference screen from Pat1's chart (Scope-P).
4. Confirm Scope-P now shows the Notification pane as well as the Reminder pane.
5. Confirm rows saved in Scope-P are stored against Pat1 only and do not appear for another patient.
6. Confirm rows saved in Scope-G apply as the clinic default and are visible from any chart that has no override.
Test Case Relevance: Prefs - scopes + notification pane added (WebIMS doc p2)

Description: Precedence: a Patient-Chart preference overrides the General default
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with a chart-level preference row for Event1 set to Mode-A; Pat2 = patient with no chart-level preference for Event1; Scope-G = General scope where Event1 is set to Mode-B.
Test Data: General: Payment failed = Email; Patient Chart (Delgado): Payment failed = Text.
Expected Output: For Delgado the Payment-failed notification uses Text (Chart wins); patients without an override use the General default.
Verification Step:
1. Set Event1 in Scope-G to Mode-B and save.
2. Open Pat1's chart scope, set Event1 to Mode-A and save.
3. Trigger Event1 for Pat1.
4. Confirm the message is delivered using Mode-A, proving the chart-level setting wins.
5. Trigger Event1 for Pat2.
6. Confirm the message is delivered using Mode-B, the General default.
7. Remove the chart override from Pat1 and trigger Event1 again; confirm Pat1 now falls back to Mode-B.
Test Case Relevance: Prefs - precedence Chart > General (WebIMS doc p2)

Description: General scope shows the "Consent to send reminder for New patients" toggle
Pre-requisite Data: Scope-G = the General (clinic) preference scope; Scope-P = the Patient Chart preference scope of any patient.
Test Data: Open General scope reminder pane.
Expected Output: The New-patient consent toggle is shown only in the General scope.
Verification Step:
1. Open the preference screen in Scope-G and go to the Reminder pane.
2. Confirm the Consent to send reminder for New patients toggle is displayed.
3. Change the toggle and save; confirm the value is retained after reopening.
4. Open the same Reminder pane in Scope-P.
5. Confirm the New-patient consent toggle is not shown at patient level.
6. Confirm no error appears in either scope because of the missing/extra toggle.
Status Comment: Not required

Description: Pay Now payment triggers the patient notification
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with an active plan Plan1 and valid contact details; Event-PS = the Payment successful notification, active, with a Mode and template configured.
Test Data: Pay Now on Delgado PP-100248 with Payment-successful active.
Expected Output: A Payment-successful notification is sent to the patient for the Pay-Now payment.
Verification Step:
1. Confirm Event-PS is active for Pat1's applicable scope.
2. Open Plan1 and collect a payment using the Pay Now option.
3. Complete the payment so it finishes successfully.
4. Confirm a Payment successful notification is generated for Pat1.
5. Confirm it is delivered on the channel(s) named in Event-PS's Mode.
6. Confirm the message content uses the Payment successful template and reflects the amount just collected.
7. Confirm only one notification is produced for the single Pay Now payment.

Description: Payment failed triggers the Payment-failed notification per configured mode
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with an active plan Plan1 whose scheduled charge is forced to fail; Event-PF = the Payment failed notification, active, Mode = All.
Test Data: Abrams PP-100377 charge Failed; Payment-failed Mode = All.
Expected Output: The Payment-failed notification is sent on all configured channels using its template.
Verification Step:
1. Configure Event-PF with Mode = All and its letter template.
2. Cause the scheduled charge on Plan1 to fail (for example an invalid or expired card).
3. Confirm the transaction is recorded with a failed status.
4. Confirm a Payment failed notification is generated for Pat1.
5. Confirm it is delivered on every channel covered by Mode = All (call, email and text as configured).
6. Confirm the message content comes from the Payment failed template.
7. Confirm no Payment successful notification is sent for the same attempt.

Description: Default letter templates for payment-plan reminders/notifications applied by default
Pre-requisite Data: DB-New = a database where the payment-plan notification/reminder events have not been customised; Event-List = the full set of payment-plan notification and reminder events.
Test Data: A fresh database with payment-plan reminder/notification events.
Expected Output: Each payment-plan reminder/notification has a default letter template applied by default (from the pain-point sheet).
Verification Step:
1. Open the preference screen on DB-New.
2. Add or open a row for each event in Event-List.
3. Confirm each row already has a default letter template selected without the user choosing one.
4. Confirm the defaulted template matches the event (for example the payment-failed event defaults to the payment-failed template).
5. Open the Template dropdown on one row and confirm other templates can still be selected instead.
6. Change the template, save, reopen and confirm the user's choice was kept over the default.
Status Comment: can select different templates from the template dropdown

Description: Add and remove rows in each pane
Pre-requisite Data: User1 = user allowed to edit preferences; Row-N = a new notification row; Row-R = a new reminder row.
Test Data: Add a notification row and a reminder row; delete one.
Expected Output: Add appends an editable row (defaulting to Payment Plan); delete removes a row.
Verification Step:
1. Log in as User1 and open the preference screen.
2. In the Notification pane click Add and confirm a new editable Row-N is appended.
3. Confirm the new row defaults its Event Type sensibly (Payment Plan) and lets the user change it.
4. In the Reminder pane click Add and confirm Row-R is appended in the same way.
5. Complete and save both rows and confirm they persist after reopening.
6. Delete Row-R and confirm it is removed from the list after saving.
7. Confirm deleting one row does not remove or alter any other row.

Description: Validation: reminder needs a Template and a valid To-Be-Sent lead time
Pre-requisite Data: Row-R = a reminder row for the Card expiry event; Template1 = a valid letter template; Lead1 = a valid numeric lead time.
Test Data: Enable Card-expiry with no template; then To-Be-Sent blank/non-numeric.
Expected Output: Blocked/flagged until a Template is chosen and a valid non-Immediate lead time is set.
Verification Step:
1. Open the Reminder pane and set Row-R active with the Card expiry event and a Mode, leaving Template blank.
2. Try to save and confirm the save is blocked or the Template field is flagged as required.
3. Select Template1 and clear the To Be Sent value; try to save and confirm it is blocked again.
4. Enter a non-numeric value in the lead-time field and confirm it is rejected or not accepted at all.
5. Enter Lead1 with a valid unit and confirm the row now saves.
6. Reopen the row and confirm Template1 and Lead1 were stored correctly.
Status Comment:
"Description: replace with:
""Required-field validation for a Payment Plan reminder row.""

Expected Output: replace with:
""A reminder row cannot be saved when required Template or required To-Be-Sent value/unit is blank for Before/After. After required values are provided, Save succeeds.""

Verification Step: replace with:
""1. Add a Payment Plan reminder row. 2. Select event and mode but leave Template blank; Save and assert blocked. 3. Select Template, choose Before/After and leave lead-time value/unit incomplete; Save and assert blocked. 4. Enter a valid lead-time value and unit and Save; assert success.""
This avoids inventing unsupported numeric min/max rules."

Description: Appointment event type still works (regression)
Pre-requisite Data: Row-APP = an existing appointment notification/reminder configuration that worked before the payment-plan events were added.
Test Data: Event Type = Appointment.
Expected Output: Original appointment events behave as before the generalization.
Verification Step:
1. Open the preference screen and set Event Type = Appointment in both panes.
2. Confirm all original appointment events are still listed.
3. Confirm Row-APP retained its Mode, To Be Sent and Template values.
4. Confirm appointment-only fields such as Visit Type and Provider are still editable here.
5. Trigger an appointment event and confirm the message is still sent as it was before.
6. Confirm adding payment-plan rows alongside does not change any appointment row's behaviour.

Description: Accessibility: keyboard-operable and screen-reader labelled
Pre-requisite Data: User1 = user with preference access; Keyboard-only navigation and a screen reader are available on the test machine.
Test Data: Keyboard-only navigation; screen reader over rows.
Expected Output: All selectors, To-Be-Sent controls, template inputs and toggles are reachable and labelled.
Verification Step:
1. Open the preference screen and navigate using only the Tab and arrow keys.
2. Confirm every Event Type, Event, Mode and Template control can be reached and operated without a mouse.
3. Confirm the To Be Sent controls (option, value and unit) are reachable and changeable by keyboard.
4. Confirm the Active toggles and Add/Delete actions are reachable and can be triggered by keyboard.
5. Confirm the focus outline is visible on every control as it is reached.
6. Run a screen reader across a row and confirm each control announces a meaningful label rather than a blank or generic name.

Description: Only authorized users can change General (clinic-level) preferences
Pre-requisite Data: User-C = user with the grant to configure General (clinic-level) preferences; User-NC = user without that grant; Pat1 = a patient chart the user may open.
Test Data: User without config grant opens General scope.
Expected Output: General preferences read-only without the grant; per-patient prefs follow chart permissions.
Verification Step:
1. Log in as User-NC and open the preference screen in the General scope.
2. Confirm the rows are read-only and no save/add/delete action is available.
3. Confirm any attempt to change a field is rejected.
4. Log in as User-C and confirm the same General rows are editable and saveable.
5. As User-NC open the Patient Chart scope of Pat1 and confirm access follows the chart permissions.
6. Confirm a user without chart access cannot open patient-level preferences at all.

Description:
Visit Type and Provider options are disabled when the Event Type is Payment Plan in the Reminder Preference screen.
- Open the Reminder Preference screen.
- Set Event Type = Payment Plan.
- Look at the Visit Type and Provider options.
Pre-requisite Data: Row-R = a reminder preference row on the Reminder Preference screen; VisitType/Provider = the appointment-specific option fields on that row.
Test Data: Reminder preference row with Event Type = Payment Plan.
Expected Output: Visit Type and Provider are disabled/greyed for Payment Plan reminders (they only apply to Appointment reminders). They remain available when Event Type = Appointment.
Verification Step:
1. Open the Reminder Preference screen.
2. On Row-R set Event Type = Payment Plan.
3. Confirm the Visit Type option is disabled/greyed and cannot be opened.
4. Confirm the Provider option is disabled/greyed and cannot be opened.
5. Confirm the row can still be saved without those two fields.
6. Change Event Type on Row-R to Appointment and confirm Visit Type and Provider become available again.
Status Comment: Visit Type/Provider disabled for Payment Plan.

Description:
The "Payment Plan setup" notification fires when a plan is created, using the configured mode.
- Configure a Payment Plan setup notification (mode Email / Text / Call / All).
- Create and activate a new patient payment plan.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with contact details; Event-PS = the Payment Plan setup notification, active, with a Mode (Email / Text / Call / All) and the setup letter template; Plan1 = a new payment plan created for Pat1.
Test Data: An active notification for "Payment Plan setup".
Expected Output: On plan creation the patient receives the Payment Plan Setup notification through the configured mode(s), using the setup letter template.
Verification Step:
1. Configure Event-PS as active with a chosen Mode and the setup template.
2. Create and activate Plan1 for Pat1.
3. Confirm a Payment Plan setup notification is generated at the moment the plan is created.
4. Confirm it is delivered only on the channel(s) named in the configured Mode.
5. Confirm the content uses the Payment Plan setup letter template and reflects Plan1's details.
6. Deactivate Event-PS, create another plan and confirm no setup notification is sent.
Status Comment: Setup notification trigger.

Description:
The "Payment plan status change" notification fires when a plan's status changes.
- Configure a "Payment plan status change" notification.
- Change a plan's status (e.g. active → inactive).
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with an active plan Plan1; Event-SC = the Payment plan status change notification, active, with a Mode and template; Status-Old and Status-New = the plan status before and after the change.
Test Data: An active status-change notification.
Expected Output: When the plan status changes, the patient receives the Status Update notification (previous status, new status, effective date) via the configured mode.
Verification Step:
1. Configure Event-SC as active with a Mode and its template.
2. Open Plan1 and change its status from Status-Old to Status-New.
3. Confirm a status-change notification is generated for Pat1.
4. Confirm the message names the previous status, the new status and the effective date.
5. Confirm it is delivered only on the configured channel(s).
6. Confirm changing the status again produces a further notification reflecting the newer values.
Status Comment: Status-change notification trigger.

Description:
The "Payment Due" reminder fires the configured lead time before the processing date.
- Configure a Payment Due reminder with a "Before" lead time (e.g. 3 days).
- Have a plan with an upcoming scheduled charge.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with active plan Plan1 having an upcoming scheduled charge on date Sched1 for amount Amt1 on card Card1; Event-PD = the Payment Due reminder, active, To Be Sent = Before with lead time Lead1.
Test Data: A Payment Due reminder set to 3 days before.
Expected Output: The patient receives the upcoming-payment reminder the configured lead time before the processing date, with the scheduled amount, processing date and card on file.
Verification Step:
1. Configure Event-PD as active with To Be Sent = Before and lead time Lead1.
2. Confirm Plan1 has an upcoming charge scheduled for Sched1.
3. Move the business date (or wait) to Sched1 minus Lead1 and run the reminder job.
4. Confirm the Payment Due reminder is sent to Pat1 on that date.
5. Confirm the message shows the scheduled amount Amt1, the processing date Sched1 and the masked card Card1.
6. Confirm no reminder is sent on any other day for the same installment.
7. Deactivate Event-PD and confirm no reminder is produced for the next installment.
Status Comment: Payment Due reminder trigger.

Description:
The "Card expiry" reminder fires the configured lead time before the card expiry (treated as the last day of the expiring month).
- Configure a Card expiry reminder with a "Before" lead time.
- Use a saved card whose expiry month is approaching.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with a plan using saved card Card1 whose expiry month is approaching; Exp-Last = the last day of Card1's expiry month; Event-CE = the Card expiry reminder, active, To Be Sent = Before with lead time Lead1.
Test Data: A card with a near expiry month.
Expected Output: The reminder fires the configured lead time before the expiry, where the expiry date is taken as the last day of the expiring month, prompting the patient to update the card. (See RPP-NRP-008 for the last-day-of-month rule.)
Verification Step:
1. Configure Event-CE as active with To Be Sent = Before and lead time Lead1.
2. Confirm Card1 is attached to Pat1's plan and its expiry month is upcoming.
3. Move the business date (or wait) to Exp-Last minus Lead1 and run the reminder job.
4. Confirm the card-expiry reminder is sent to Pat1 on that date.
5. Confirm the expiry date used is Exp-Last, the last day of the expiring month.
6. Confirm the message asks the patient to update the card and identifies the card in masked form.
7. Confirm no reminder is sent for a card whose expiry is far outside the lead time.
Status Comment: Card expiry reminder trigger.

Description: [New] The new Agreement event is available in the notification preference event list
Pre-requisite Data: User1 = user allowed to edit notification preferences; Clinic1 = clinic where the payment-plan agreement feature is switched on.
Test Data: Open the Notification pane, set Event Type = Payment Plan and open the Event dropdown.
Expected Output: The Event list now includes the Agreement event alongside the existing payment-plan notification events, and it can be selected and saved like any other event.
Verification Step:
1. Log in as User1 and open the Notification and Reminder Preference screen for Clinic1.
2. In the Notification pane set Event Type = Payment Plan.
3. Open the Event dropdown and confirm an Agreement event is listed.
4. Select the Agreement event and confirm the Mode and Template fields become available for it.
5. Save the row and reopen the screen; confirm the Agreement row persists with its Mode and Template.
6. Confirm the existing payment-plan events are still listed and unaffected by the new entry.

Description: [New] Clicking Agree & Continue on the payment plan agreement sends the agreement email when the event is configured
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with a valid email address; Plan1 = a payment plan for Pat1 that shows the agreement window on save; Event-AG = the Agreement notification, active, Mode includes Email, with the agreement template selected.
Test Data: Configure Event-AG as active with Email in its Mode, save Plan1 for Pat1 and click Agree & Continue on the agreement window.
Expected Output: As soon as the user clicks Agree & Continue, an agreement email is sent to the patient using the configured agreement template, and the plan is activated as usual.
Verification Step:
1. Configure Event-AG as active with Email included in its Mode and the agreement template selected.
2. Save Plan1 for Pat1 so the agreement window is presented.
3. Click Agree & Continue on the agreement window.
4. Confirm the plan is activated and the agreement is recorded against Pat1.
5. Open Pat1's mailbox or the outgoing mail log and confirm an agreement email was sent at that moment.
6. Confirm the email content comes from the configured agreement template and carries the agreement document.
7. Confirm only one agreement email was sent for the single Agree & Continue click.

Description: [New] No agreement email is sent when the Agreement event is inactive or not configured
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with a valid email address; Plan1 = a payment plan for Pat1 that shows the agreement window; Event-AG = the Agreement notification row left inactive or not created at all.
Test Data: With Event-AG inactive, save Plan1 and click Agree & Continue on the agreement window.
Expected Output: The plan is activated and the agreement is recorded, but no agreement email leaves the system because the event is not configured to send.
Verification Step:
1. Confirm Event-AG is either absent or marked inactive in the notification preference.
2. Save Plan1 for Pat1 so the agreement window is presented.
3. Click Agree & Continue.
4. Confirm the plan is activated and the agreement is stored against Pat1.
5. Check Pat1's mailbox and the outgoing mail log and confirm no agreement email was produced.
6. Activate Event-AG, repeat the agreement on another plan and confirm the email is then sent, proving the switch controls the behaviour.

Description: [New] The Agreement event honours its configured Mode (All / Call / Email / Text)
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with a valid email address and mobile number; Event-AG = the Agreement notification row; Mode-X = the mode under test (All, Call, Email or Text); Plan1 = a plan for Pat1 that shows the agreement window.
Test Data: Set Event-AG to Mode-X, agree on Plan1 and check which channels were used; repeat for each mode value.
Expected Output: The agreement message goes out only on the channel(s) named by Mode-X, and Mode = All delivers on every configured channel.
Verification Step:
1. Set Event-AG active with Mode = Email, agree on a plan and confirm only an email is sent.
2. Set Mode = Text, agree on another plan and confirm only a text message is sent.
3. Set Mode = Call, agree on another plan and confirm only the call/voice channel is used.
4. Set Mode = All, agree on another plan and confirm every configured channel receives the message.
5. Confirm no channel outside the selected Mode is ever used.
6. Confirm the same agreement template is used regardless of the Mode chosen.

Description: [New] Switching the Event Type back to Appointment re-enables the Visit Type and Provider options
Pre-requisite Data: Row-R = a reminder preference row on the Reminder Preference screen; VisitType1 = any selectable visit type; Provider1 = any selectable provider.
Test Data: On Row-R switch Event Type from Appointment to Payment Plan and back to Appointment, watching the Visit Type and Provider fields each time.
Expected Output: The two fields are disabled while Event Type = Payment Plan and become fully usable again the moment the event type is switched back to Appointment.
Verification Step:
1. Open the Reminder Preference screen and set Row-R's Event Type = Appointment.
2. Confirm Visit Type and Provider are enabled and can be opened.
3. Switch Event Type to Payment Plan and confirm both fields become disabled/greyed.
4. Switch Event Type back to Appointment.
5. Confirm Visit Type and Provider are enabled again and VisitType1 and Provider1 can be selected.
6. Save the row and confirm the appointment row keeps the selected visit type and provider.
7. Confirm switching event type does not raise any error or blank out the rest of the row.

Description: [New] A saved Payment Plan reminder row never stores a visit type or provider value
Pre-requisite Data: Row-R = a reminder row first set to Event Type = Appointment with VisitType1 and Provider1 chosen, then switched to Event Type = Payment Plan before saving.
Test Data: Choose VisitType1 and Provider1 on an appointment row, switch the row to Payment Plan, save it and reopen the screen.
Expected Output: The saved Payment Plan row carries no visit type and no provider — the earlier selections are cleared, not silently kept in the background.
Verification Step:
1. Open the Reminder Preference screen and set Row-R to Event Type = Appointment.
2. Select VisitType1 and Provider1 on the row.
3. Switch Row-R's Event Type to Payment Plan and confirm the two fields become disabled.
4. Save the row.
5. Reopen the preference screen and confirm the Payment Plan row shows no visit type and no provider value.
6. Switch the saved row back to Appointment and confirm the fields come back empty rather than pre-filled with the old selections.
7. Confirm the reminder fires for all applicable patients, proving it was not silently filtered by a hidden visit type or provider.

Description: [New] The Immediate option is not selectable (greyed/absent) for a Payment Plan reminder row
Pre-requisite Data: Row-R = a reminder row with Event Type = Payment Plan and any payment-plan reminder event selected.
Test Data: On Row-R open the To Be Sent option list and try to pick Immediate.
Expected Output: Immediate cannot be chosen for a Payment Plan reminder — it is greyed out or not listed — and only After and Before with a lead time can be saved.
Verification Step:
1. Open the Reminder pane and set Row-R's Event Type = Payment Plan.
2. Open the To Be Sent option list.
3. Confirm Immediate is either absent or shown greyed and cannot be clicked.
4. Confirm After and Before remain selectable together with their value and unit fields.
5. Attempt to save the row with Immediate (if it can be forced) and confirm the save is blocked with a clear message.
6. Save the row with Before and a lead time and confirm it stores correctly.
7. Reopen the row and confirm the To Be Sent option is still not Immediate.

Description: [New] Switching a reminder row from Payment Plan to Appointment restores the Immediate option
Pre-requisite Data: Row-R = a reminder row currently set to Event Type = Payment Plan where Immediate is restricted.
Test Data: Switch Row-R's Event Type from Payment Plan to Appointment and reopen the To Be Sent option list.
Expected Output: Immediate becomes available again as soon as the event type is Appointment, and the row can be saved with Immediate for an appointment reminder.
Verification Step:
1. Open Row-R with Event Type = Payment Plan and confirm Immediate is not selectable.
2. Switch Event Type to Appointment.
3. Open the To Be Sent option list and confirm Immediate is now available.
4. Select Immediate and confirm the value and unit fields are hidden or disabled as designed.
5. Save the appointment row with Immediate and confirm it saves successfully.
6. Switch the row back to Payment Plan and confirm Immediate is restricted again and the row cannot be saved with it.

Description: [New] Card expiry is taken as the last day of the expiry month for a 31-day and a 30-day month
Pre-requisite Data: Card-31 = saved card whose expiry month has 31 days; Card-30 = saved card whose expiry month has 30 days; Event-CE = the Card expiry reminder, active, To Be Sent = Before with lead time Lead1.
Test Data: Attach Card-31 and Card-30 to payment plans and run the card-expiry reminder with lead time Lead1.
Expected Output: The expiry date used is the 31st for Card-31 and the 30th for Card-30 — always the last calendar day of the stored expiry month — and each reminder fires Lead1 before that date.
Verification Step:
1. Configure Event-CE active with To Be Sent = Before and lead time Lead1.
2. Attach Card-31 to a plan and Card-30 to another plan.
3. Move the business date to the last day of Card-31's expiry month minus Lead1 and run the reminder job.
4. Confirm the reminder for Card-31 is sent on that date and not on any earlier day of the month.
5. Repeat for Card-30 using the last day of its 30-day expiry month minus Lead1.
6. Confirm the reminder for Card-30 is sent on that date.
7. Confirm neither card is treated as expiring on the first day of its expiry month.

Description: [New] Card expiry in February is taken as the last day of February, including a leap year
Pre-requisite Data: Card-Feb = saved card expiring in a February of a non-leap year; Card-Leap = saved card expiring in a February of a leap year; Event-CE = the Card expiry reminder, active, To Be Sent = Before with lead time Lead1.
Test Data: Run the card-expiry reminder for plans holding Card-Feb and Card-Leap.
Expected Output: The expiry date is the 28th for the non-leap February and the 29th for the leap February, and each reminder fires Lead1 days before the correct last day.
Verification Step:
1. Configure Event-CE active with To Be Sent = Before and lead time Lead1.
2. Attach Card-Feb to one plan and Card-Leap to another.
3. Move the business date to the last day of Card-Feb's February minus Lead1 and run the job.
4. Confirm the reminder for Card-Feb is sent on that date, using the 28th as the expiry date.
5. Repeat for Card-Leap and confirm the 29th is used as the expiry date.
6. Confirm neither reminder is sent a day early or a day late because of the month length.
7. Confirm no error occurs while calculating the February expiry date.

Description: [New] A card expiring in the current month is still treated as valid until the last day of that month
Pre-requisite Data: Card-Now = saved card whose expiry month is the current month; Exp-Last = the last day of the current month; Plan1 = an active plan using Card-Now with an installment scheduled before Exp-Last.
Test Data: Run the scheduled charge for Plan1 on a date inside the current month and observe the card treatment and the reminder.
Expected Output: Card-Now is treated as valid up to and including Exp-Last, so a charge before that date is attempted normally, and the expiry reminder is timed against Exp-Last.
Verification Step:
1. Confirm Card-Now's expiry month is the current month and Plan1 uses it.
2. Run the scheduled charge on a date earlier than Exp-Last.
3. Confirm the card is not rejected as expired by the system's own expiry check.
4. Confirm the card-expiry reminder is timed against Exp-Last and not against the first day of the month.
5. Move the business date past Exp-Last and confirm the card is then treated as expired.
6. Confirm a charge attempted after Exp-Last is recorded as failed and the installment turns Overdue on the plan.

Description: [New] Both notification and reminder emails for payment plans go out from the clinic's email setup
Pre-requisite Data: Clinic1 = clinic with a configured outgoing email setup Email1; Pat1 = patient with a valid email address; Event-N = any payment-plan notification with Email in its Mode; Event-R = any payment-plan reminder with Email in its Mode.
Test Data: Trigger Event-N and Event-R for Pat1 and inspect the sender address of both emails.
Expected Output: Both the notification email and the reminder email show the clinic's configured sender address from Email1, never a system default or an individual user's address.
Verification Step:
1. Confirm Clinic1's outgoing email setup Email1 is active and note its sender address.
2. Configure Event-N and Event-R with Email included in their Mode.
3. Trigger Event-N for Pat1 and open the resulting email.
4. Confirm its sender address is the one from Email1.
5. Trigger Event-R for Pat1 and open the resulting email.
6. Confirm its sender address is also the one from Email1.
7. Confirm no email uses a generic system address or the logged-in user's personal address.

Description: [New] Changing the clinic email setup changes the sender of subsequent payment-plan emails
Pre-requisite Data: Clinic1 = clinic whose outgoing email setup is first Email1 and later changed to Email2; Pat1 = patient with a valid email address; Event-N = a payment-plan notification with Email in its Mode.
Test Data: Trigger Event-N with Email1 configured, change the clinic setup to Email2, then trigger Event-N again.
Expected Output: Emails sent before the change carry Email1's sender and emails sent after the change carry Email2's sender, with no restart or manual re-selection needed.
Verification Step:
1. With Email1 configured, trigger Event-N for Pat1 and confirm the sender is Email1's address.
2. Change Clinic1's outgoing email setup to Email2 and save.
3. Trigger Event-N again for Pat1.
4. Confirm the new email's sender is Email2's address.
5. Confirm the earlier email still shows Email1 in the mail log, unaltered.
6. Confirm the same behaviour applies to a reminder email triggered after the change.

Description: [New] Every payment-plan notification/reminder event row comes with its default letter template preselected
Pre-requisite Data: Event-List = the full set of payment-plan notification and reminder events, including Payment Successful, Payment Failed, Payment Plan Setup, Payment Plan Status Change, Payment Due, Card Expiry and Agreement; DB1 = a database where no template customisation has been done.
Test Data: On DB1, add a preference row for each event in Event-List and read the Template field before touching it.
Expected Output: Each event row already shows its matching default letter template without the user selecting one, and the user can still switch to another template if needed.
Verification Step:
1. Open the preference screen on DB1.
2. Add a row and select the first event from Event-List.
3. Confirm the Template field is already filled with a default template and is not blank.
4. Confirm the defaulted template matches the chosen event by name/content.
5. Repeat steps 2 to 4 for every remaining event in Event-List, including the new Agreement event.
6. On one row open the Template dropdown and confirm other templates are selectable.
7. Change that template, save, reopen and confirm the user's choice was kept instead of the default.

Description: [New] The default payment-plan letter templates are present in every database by default
Pre-requisite Data: DB-A and DB-B = two different databases/clinics where no manual template setup has been performed; Event-List = the payment-plan notification and reminder events.
Test Data: Open the template list and the preference screen on DB-A and then on DB-B and compare the available default templates.
Expected Output: Both databases already contain the default letter templates for every payment-plan reminder/notification event, so no clinic has to create them manually.
Verification Step:
1. Open the letter template list on DB-A and confirm a default template exists for each event in Event-List.
2. Open the preference screen on DB-A and confirm each event row defaults to its template.
3. Repeat steps 1 and 2 on DB-B.
4. Confirm the same set of default templates is present on both databases.
5. Confirm the templates are usable immediately without further configuration.
6. Confirm a clinic-specific edit on DB-A does not change the template on DB-B.

Description: [New] End-to-end: the Payment Successful notification fires on a successful scheduled charge using its configured mode
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with contact details and active plan Plan1; Event-PS = the Payment successful notification, active, with Mode-X and its default template.
Test Data: Let a scheduled charge on Plan1 complete successfully with Event-PS configured as Mode-X.
Expected Output: The patient receives the Payment Successful message on exactly the channels named in Mode-X, with the amount and the payment/confirmation number of the transaction.
Verification Step:
1. Configure Event-PS active with Mode-X and its default template.
2. Let the scheduled charge on Plan1 run and complete successfully.
3. Confirm the transaction is recorded with a successful status.
4. Confirm the Payment Successful message reaches Pat1 on the channel(s) of Mode-X only.
5. Confirm the message shows the paid amount and the confirmation/payment number of that transaction.
6. Confirm exactly one message per configured channel is sent for the single successful charge.
7. Deactivate Event-PS, run another successful charge and confirm no message is sent.

Description: [New] End-to-end: the Payment Failed notification fires on a failed charge using its configured mode
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with contact details and active plan Plan1 on a card that will be declined; Event-PF = the Payment failed notification, active, with Mode-X and its default template.
Test Data: Let a scheduled charge on Plan1 fail with Event-PF configured as Mode-X.
Expected Output: The patient receives the Payment Failed message only on the channels named in Mode-X, and no success message is produced for the same attempt.
Verification Step:
1. Configure Event-PF active with Mode-X and its default template.
2. Let the scheduled charge on Plan1 fail.
3. Confirm the transaction is recorded as failed in Payment Transaction Tracking.
4. Confirm the Payment Failed message reaches Pat1 on the channel(s) of Mode-X only.
5. Confirm the message content comes from the payment-failed template and refers to the missed installment.
6. Confirm no Payment Successful message was sent for the same attempt.
7. Confirm the installment shows Overdue on the plan after the failure.

Description: [New] End-to-end: the Payment Plan Setup notification fires on plan creation using its configured mode
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with contact details; Event-PSU = the Payment Plan setup notification, active, with Mode-X and its default template; Plan-New = a plan created and activated for Pat1.
Test Data: Create and activate Plan-New for Pat1 with Event-PSU configured as Mode-X.
Expected Output: The setup message is delivered on the Mode-X channels at the moment the plan is created, carrying the plan's schedule details from the setup template.
Verification Step:
1. Configure Event-PSU active with Mode-X and its default template.
2. Create and activate Plan-New for Pat1.
3. Confirm the setup message is generated at the moment the plan is created.
4. Confirm it is delivered only on the channel(s) of Mode-X.
5. Confirm the content comes from the setup template and reflects Plan-New's amount, frequency and start date.
6. Confirm editing the plan afterwards does not resend the setup message.
7. Deactivate Event-PSU, create another plan and confirm no setup message is sent.

Description: [New] End-to-end: the Payment Plan Status Change notification fires on every plan status change using its configured mode
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with contact details and plan Plan1; Event-SC = the Payment plan status change notification, active, with Mode-X; Status-Old / Status-New = the plan status before and after the change.
Test Data: Change Plan1's status from Status-Old to Status-New with Event-SC configured as Mode-X.
Expected Output: Each status change sends one message on the Mode-X channels naming the old status, the new status and the effective date.
Verification Step:
1. Configure Event-SC active with Mode-X and its default template.
2. Change Plan1's status from Status-Old to Status-New.
3. Confirm one status-change message is generated for Pat1.
4. Confirm it is delivered only on the channel(s) of Mode-X.
5. Confirm the message names Status-Old, Status-New and the effective date.
6. Change the status a second time and confirm a further message with the newer values is sent.
7. Confirm a change that does not alter the status (a plain save) does not send a message.

Description: [New] End-to-end: the Payment Due reminder fires before the processing date using its configured mode
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with contact details and plan Plan1 having an upcoming charge on Sched1 for Amt1 on card Card1; Event-PD = the Payment Due reminder, active, Mode-X, To Be Sent = Before with lead time Lead1.
Test Data: Run the reminder job on Sched1 minus Lead1 with Event-PD configured as Mode-X.
Expected Output: The patient is reminded on the Mode-X channels exactly Lead1 before Sched1, with the upcoming amount, the processing date and the card on file.
Verification Step:
1. Configure Event-PD active with Mode-X, To Be Sent = Before and lead time Lead1.
2. Confirm Plan1 has an upcoming charge on Sched1.
3. Move the business date to Sched1 minus Lead1 and run the reminder job.
4. Confirm the reminder reaches Pat1 only on the channel(s) of Mode-X.
5. Confirm the message shows Amt1, the processing date Sched1 and the masked Card1.
6. Confirm no reminder is sent on any other day for the same installment.
7. Confirm the reminder is not sent for an installment that has already been paid early.

Description: [New] End-to-end: the Card Expiry reminder fires before the last day of the expiry month using its configured mode
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with contact details and plan Plan1 on saved card Card1; Exp-Last = the last day of Card1's expiry month; Event-CE = the Card expiry reminder, active, Mode-X, To Be Sent = Before with lead time Lead1.
Test Data: Run the reminder job on Exp-Last minus Lead1 with Event-CE configured as Mode-X.
Expected Output: The patient is reminded on the Mode-X channels exactly Lead1 before Exp-Last and is asked to update the card before it expires.
Verification Step:
1. Configure Event-CE active with Mode-X, To Be Sent = Before and lead time Lead1.
2. Confirm Card1 is attached to Plan1 and its expiry month is upcoming.
3. Move the business date to Exp-Last minus Lead1 and run the reminder job.
4. Confirm the reminder reaches Pat1 only on the channel(s) of Mode-X.
5. Confirm the expiry date used in the calculation and the message is Exp-Last.
6. Confirm the message identifies the card in masked form and asks for an update.
7. Replace the card with a valid one and confirm no further expiry reminder is sent for the old card.

Description: [New] End-to-end: the Agreement event fires when the patient agrees, honouring its configured mode
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with contact details; Plan1 = a plan for Pat1 that presents the agreement window on save; Event-AG = the Agreement notification, active, with Mode-X and the agreement template.
Test Data: Save Plan1, click Agree & Continue on the agreement window with Event-AG configured as Mode-X.
Expected Output: The agreement message goes out on the Mode-X channels as soon as the user agrees, carrying the agreement document/content, and nothing is sent if the agreement window is closed without agreeing.
Verification Step:
1. Configure Event-AG active with Mode-X and the agreement template.
2. Save Plan1 for Pat1 so the agreement window is shown.
3. Click Agree & Continue.
4. Confirm the agreement message is delivered only on the channel(s) of Mode-X.
5. Confirm the email carries the agreement document/content from the agreement template.
6. Create another plan, close the agreement window without agreeing and confirm no agreement message is sent.
7. Reopen the agreement from the Agreement button, agree, and confirm the message is then sent.

Description: [New] An inactive payment-plan notification/reminder row sends nothing while an active one with Mode = All sends on every channel
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with contact details and an active plan; Event-Off = a payment-plan event row saved with Active unticked; Event-All = another payment-plan event row saved as active with Mode = All.
Test Data: Trigger both Event-Off and Event-All for Pat1 and compare what is delivered.
Expected Output: Event-Off produces no message at all, while Event-All delivers on every configured channel (call, email and text) for the same patient.
Verification Step:
1. Save Event-Off with Active unticked and Event-All as active with Mode = All.
2. Trigger the situation that would fire Event-Off.
3. Confirm no message of any kind is sent to Pat1 for that event.
4. Trigger the situation that fires Event-All.
5. Confirm the message is delivered on every channel covered by Mode = All.
6. Tick Active on Event-Off, trigger it again and confirm it now sends, proving the Active flag is what controls it.
7. Confirm no other patient receives messages from either trigger.

Description:
Agreement template renders all five sections in order.
- Open the Agreement preview on the patient payment plan setup screen.
- Confirm the sections present.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with a saved recurring payment plan Plan1; Plan1 = plan with a saved card Card1 and a complete Due On schedule; Client setting "Show Agreement on Payment Plan" = Yes (mandatory or non-mandatory) so the Agreement is available; Tpl1 = the default Payment Plan Agreement letter template applied to the database.
Test Data: A payment plan with card + schedule details.
Expected Output: The Agreement shows: Payment Details, Terms & Conditions, Cancellation Policy, Electronic Communications Consent, and Execution & Authorization (with the "Agree & Continue" checkbox), in that order.
Verification Step: 1. Log in and open Pat1 > Payment Plan and open Plan1 in the patient payment plan setup screen. 2. Click the Agreement button / save the plan so the Agreement preview opens. 3. Read the section headings from top to bottom and assert they appear in this order: Payment Details, Terms & Conditions, Cancellation Policy, Electronic Communications Consent, Execution & Authorization. 4. Assert none of the five sections is missing, duplicated or out of order. 5. Assert the Execution & Authorization section contains the "Agree & Continue" checkbox/button. 6. Scroll to the very bottom and confirm no unexpected extra section is rendered after Execution & Authorization. 7. Close and re-open the Agreement for Plan1 and confirm the same five sections render in the same order.
Status Comment: Agreement template structure (Agreement.pdf).

Description:
Agreement Payment Details merge fields populate from the plan.
- Open the Agreement preview for a plan with a saved card and an end date.
- Check each Payment Details line.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with e-mail Email1 and mobile number Phone1 on the demographics screen; Plan1 = saved payment plan for Pat1 with recurring amount Amt1, frequency Freq1, an End Date End1 and a saved card Card1; Card1 = card with a brand, a last-4 and an expiry month/year; Total1 = the total authorized amount of Plan1.
Test Data: Amount, Frequency, card Brand+last 4+expiry, email/phone, Total Authorized, End Date all present.
Expected Output: Payment Details shows the real values: Payment Amount, Payment Frequency, Payment Method (Brand ending in <last 4> | Exp <date>), Patient Email/Text, Total Authorized Amount, and End Date — each filled from the plan, no leftover <placeholders>.
Verification Step: 1. Open Pat1 > Payment Plan, open Plan1 and launch the Agreement preview. 2. In the Payment Details section, assert Payment Amount equals Amt1 as saved on Plan1. 3. Assert Payment Frequency equals Freq1 exactly as configured in the Due On section. 4. Assert Payment Method shows Card1 brand + "ending in" its last 4 digits + its expiry, and that the full card number is never shown. 5. Assert Patient Email/Text show Email1 and Phone1 from Pat1 demographics. 6. Assert Total Authorized Amount equals Total1 and End Date equals End1. 7. Scan the whole Payment Details block and assert no un-merged placeholder token (any text still wrapped in angle brackets or braces) is left on screen.
Status Comment: Agreement merge fields.

Description:
Agreement notes that if the remaining balance is less than the payment amount, the final payment is only the remaining balance.
- Read the Payment Amount line in the Agreement.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with saved payment plan Plan1; Plan1 = plan with "Deduct amount only if patient has balance" ticked, recurring amount Amt1; Agreement available for Plan1 per the client setting.
Test Data: Any plan.
Expected Output: The Agreement states that if the remaining balance is less than the recurring amount, the final payment will be for the remaining balance only — matching the deduct-if-balance last-installment rule (RPP-PLAN-024).
Verification Step: 1. Open Pat1 > Payment Plan > Plan1 and launch the Agreement preview. 2. Locate the Payment Amount line inside Payment Details. 3. Assert the wording states that if the remaining balance is less than the recurring amount, the final payment will be for the remaining balance only. 4. Assert this clause is present even when Plan1 has no End Date. 5. Confirm the clause matches the deduct-if-balance last-installment behaviour described for the plan (no contradicting wording elsewhere in the Agreement). 6. Confirm the clause text is static template wording and is not replaced by a numeric value.
Status Comment: Agreement final-payment clause.

Description:
Agreement Terms: a separate manual payment does not stop, reduce, or delay the next scheduled auto payment.
- Read the Manual Payments clause under Terms & Conditions.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with saved payment plan Plan1; Agreement available for Plan1 per the client setting; Tpl1 = the default Payment Plan Agreement template applied to the database.
Test Data: Any plan.
Expected Output: The Manual Payments clause clearly states a separate manual payment will not automatically stop, reduce, or delay the next scheduled automatic payment.
