Description:
Payment Plan Setup letter (Email + Text) populates correctly; the outstanding-balance line shows only when an end date exists.
- Trigger the Payment Plan Setup notification for a plan WITH an end date, then for one WITHOUT.
- Check both the Email and Text versions.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with e-mail Email1 and mobile Phone1; Plan1 = saved payment plan for Pat1 WITH an End Date; Plan2 = saved payment plan (same or another patient) WITHOUT an End Date; Notification preference for the Payment Plan Setup event is enabled for both Email and Text; Tpl1 = default Payment Plan Setup letter template.
Test Data: One plan with an end date; one without.
Expected Output: The Email shows recurring amount, frequency, first payment date and payment method; the Text is the short version. The "Total Outstanding Balance" line appears only when the plan has an end date, and is omitted otherwise.
Verification Step: 1. Enable the Payment Plan Setup notification (Email + Text) in the notification preference for the Payment Plan event type. 2. Save Plan1 so the setup notification is triggered, then open the generated Email in the notification/communication log. 3. Assert the Email shows the recurring amount, the frequency, the first payment date and the payment method of Plan1. 4. Assert the Email for Plan1 contains the Total Outstanding Balance line. 5. Open the Text version for Plan1 and assert it carries the same key facts in short form. 6. Repeat for Plan2 (no End Date) and assert the Total Outstanding Balance line is NOT present in either the Email or the Text. 7. Assert no un-merged placeholder tokens remain in either letter.
Status Comment: Setup template Email+Text + conditional balance.

Description:
Payment Plan Status Update letter (Email + Text) shows previous status, new status and effective date; balance line only with an end date.
- Trigger the Status Update notification after a status change.
- Check Email and Text.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with an active payment plan Plan1 that has an End Date; Plan2 = payment plan without an End Date; Status1 = the status of the plan before the change; Status2 = the status after the change; Notification preference for the Payment Plan Status Change event enabled for Email and Text.
Test Data: A plan whose status changed.
Expected Output: The letter shows Previous Status, New Status and Effective Date, plus a Remaining Balance line only when an end date exists. The Text version carries the short "status changed to <status> on <date>" message.
Verification Step: 1. Enable the Payment Plan Status Change notification (Email + Text). 2. Change Plan1 status from Status1 to Status2 and save. 3. Open the generated Email from the notification log. 4. Assert it shows Previous Status = Status1, New Status = Status2 and an Effective Date equal to the date the change was made. 5. Assert the Remaining Balance line is present because Plan1 has an End Date. 6. Open the Text version and assert it carries the short "status changed to <new status> on <date>" message with the same values. 7. Repeat the status change on Plan2 and assert the Remaining Balance line is omitted. 8. Assert no un-merged placeholder tokens remain.
Status Comment: Status-update template.

Description:
Payment Successful letter (Email + Text) shows amount, date, method, confirmation number; plan balance only with an end date.
- Trigger the Payment Successful notification after a successful charge.
- Check Email and Text.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with payment plan Plan1 (End Date set) and saved card Card1; Plan2 = plan without an End Date; Amt1 = the installment amount charged; Notification preference for the Payment Successful event enabled for Email and Text; a successful charge exists on Plan1.
Test Data: A successful plan charge.
Expected Output: The letter shows Amount Paid, Date Processed, Payment Method (brand + last 4 + expiry), Confirmation Number, and a Remaining Plan Balance line only when an end date exists.
Verification Step: 1. Enable the Payment Successful notification (Email + Text). 2. Run or trigger a successful charge on Plan1 (scheduled run or Pay Now). 3. Open the generated Email from the notification log. 4. Assert Amount Paid equals the amount actually charged, and Date Processed equals the date of the successful transaction. 5. Assert Payment Method shows Card1 brand + last 4 + expiry only (never the full card number). 6. Assert a Confirmation Number is present and not blank. 7. Assert the Remaining Plan Balance line is shown for Plan1 (End Date exists) and is omitted after a successful charge on Plan2. 8. Open the Text version and assert it repeats amount and date consistently.
Status Comment: Payment-successful template.

Description:
Payment Failed letter (Email + Text) states the failed amount/date, the retry timing, and next steps.
- Trigger the Payment Failed notification after a declined charge.
- Check Email and Text.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with payment plan Plan1 and a card Card1 that will be declined by the gateway; Notification preference for the Payment Failed event enabled for Email and Text; Retry1 = the configured retry interval.
Test Data: A failed plan charge.
Expected Output: The letter states the payment could not be processed, that it will be retried after the configured time, and next steps (call the clinic to update details). The Text version is the short "Payment of $ on <date> failed" message.
Verification Step: 1. Enable the Payment Failed notification (Email + Text). 2. Force a scheduled charge on Plan1 to be declined by the gateway. 3. Open the generated Email from the notification log. 4. Assert it states the payment could not be processed and shows the failed amount and the failed date. 5. Assert it states the payment will be retried after the configured retry time Retry1. 6. Assert it gives next steps (contact the clinic to update payment details). 7. Open the Text version and assert it carries the short failed-payment message with the same amount and date. 8. Assert the letter does not expose full card details.
Status Comment: Payment-failed template.

Description:
Card Expiring reminder (Email + Text) shows the card last 4 and treats the expiry as the last day of the expiring month.
- Trigger the Card Expiring reminder for a card whose month is ending.
- Check Email and Text.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with payment plan Plan1 using card Card1; Card1 = saved card whose expiry month/year is the month about to end; Notification preference for the Card Expiry reminder enabled for Email and Text; the Card Expiry reminder schedule is due to run.
Test Data: A card nearing expiry.
Expected Output: The reminder shows the card ending in <last 4> and states it expires on the last day of the expiring month, prompting the patient to update the card to avoid a payment failure.
Verification Step: 1. Enable the Card Expiry reminder (Email + Text) in the notification/reminder preference. 2. Let the Card Expiry reminder run for Plan1 / Card1. 3. Open the generated Email from the notification log. 4. Assert it identifies the card as "ending in" the last 4 digits of Card1 and never shows the full number. 5. Assert the expiry date printed in the letter is the LAST day of Card1 expiry month (not the first day and not the raw month/year only). 6. Assert the letter prompts the patient to update the card to avoid a payment failure. 7. Open the Text version and assert the same last-4 and the same expiry date are used. 8. Assert no un-merged placeholder tokens remain.
Status Comment: Card-expiry template + last-day rule.

Description:
Payment Due reminder (Email + Text) shows the scheduled amount, processing date, method, and "in X days".
- Trigger the Payment Due reminder ahead of a scheduled charge.
- Check Email and Text.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with an active payment plan Plan1 with an upcoming scheduled charge on date Due1 and saved card Card1; Amt1 = the scheduled installment amount; Lead1 = the configured number of days before the due date at which the Payment Due reminder runs; notification preference for the Payment Due reminder enabled for Email and Text.
Test Data: An upcoming scheduled charge.
Expected Output: The reminder shows the Scheduled Amount, Processing Date, and the Payment Method on file, and states the auto-payment will be processed in X days with no action needed if details are up to date.
Verification Step: 1. Enable the Payment Due reminder (Email + Text) with lead time Lead1. 2. Let the reminder run Lead1 days before Due1 for Plan1. 3. Open the generated Email from the notification log. 4. Assert the Scheduled Amount equals Amt1 and the Processing Date equals Due1. 5. Assert the Payment Method on file shows Card1 brand + last 4 only. 6. Assert the letter states the auto-payment will be processed in the correct number of days and that no action is needed if details are up to date. 7. Open the Text version and assert amount and date match the Email. 8. Assert no un-merged placeholder tokens remain.
Status Comment: Payment-due template.

Description:
Across all letters, balance/outstanding lines appear only when the plan has an end date, and the clinic email setup is the sender.
- Trigger any two payment-plan letters — one for a plan with an end date, one without.
- Check the balance lines and the email sender.
Pre-requisite Data: Plan1 = payment plan WITH an End Date; Plan2 = payment plan WITHOUT an End Date; Office1 = the clinic whose e-mail setup is configured with sender address Sender1; notification preferences for at least two payment-plan letter events enabled for Email.
Test Data: One plan with an end date; one without.
Expected Output: Any "Total Outstanding / Remaining Balance" line is shown only when the plan has an end date (omitted for open-ended plans). All payment-plan emails are sent from the clinic's configured email setup.
Verification Step: 1. Configure Office1 e-mail setup with sender address Sender1. 2. Trigger any payment-plan letter for Plan1 and open the generated Email. 3. Assert the "Total Outstanding / Remaining Balance" line is present because Plan1 has an End Date. 4. Trigger the same letter for Plan2 and assert the balance line is completely omitted (no empty label, no zero value). 5. Repeat steps 2-4 with a second payment-plan letter type to prove the rule is template-wide. 6. Inspect the From address of every generated Email and assert it equals Sender1 from the Office1 e-mail setup, not a user mailbox or a hard-coded system address. 7. Confirm the same sender is used for both the with-end-date and no-end-date letters.
Status Comment: Conditional balance + clinic-email sender across templates.

Description: [New] Confirmation Number in the Payment Successful letter is filled with the payment number generated for the credit-card transaction.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with an active payment plan Plan1 paid by saved card Card1; PayNo1 = the payment number the system generates for a credit-card transaction of Plan1; notification preference for the Payment Successful event enabled for Email.
Test Data: Run one successful credit-card charge on Plan1; note PayNo1 from the transaction/receipt record.
Expected Output: The Confirmation Number merge field in the Payment Successful letter is populated with PayNo1 — the payment number generated for that credit-card transaction — and not with the plan number, the installment number or a blank value.
Verification Step: 1. Enable the Payment Successful notification (Email) for the Payment Plan event type. 2. Open Pat1 > Payment Plan > Plan1 and run a successful credit-card charge (scheduled run or Pay Now). 3. Open the created receipt / Transaction Tracking row for that charge and note the generated payment number PayNo1. 4. Open the Payment Successful Email produced for that charge from the notification log. 5. Assert the Confirmation Number field is not blank and its value is exactly PayNo1. 6. Assert the Confirmation Number is NOT the payment plan number, the installment number or the receipt sequence of some other transaction. 7. Run a second successful charge on Plan1 and assert the new letter carries the NEW payment number, proving the field is per-transaction.

Description: [New] Confirmation Number in the Payment Successful letter matches the payment number shown on Transaction Tracking for the same charge.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with active payment plan Plan1 and saved card Card1; PayNo1 = payment number of the credit-card transaction; Transaction Tracking screen accessible for Plan1.
Test Data: One successful credit-card charge on Plan1; compare the letter against the Transaction Tracking row.
Expected Output: The Confirmation Number printed in the letter is identical to the payment number displayed for the same transaction on the Transaction Tracking screen, so the patient can quote it to the clinic.
Verification Step: 1. Run a successful credit-card charge on Plan1. 2. Open Transaction Tracking filtered to Plan1 and locate the row for that charge. 3. Note the payment number PayNo1 on that row. 4. Open the Payment Successful Email for the same charge. 5. Assert the Confirmation Number equals PayNo1 character for character. 6. Assert the letter amount and date also match the same Transaction Tracking row. 7. Repeat for a second charge and confirm each letter maps to its own transaction row.

Description: [New] A Pay Now credit-card payment also produces a Payment Successful letter carrying that Pay Now transaction payment number.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with a saved payment plan Plan1 and saved card Card1; PayNo1 = payment number generated for the Pay Now credit-card transaction; Payment Successful notification enabled for Email and Text.
Test Data: Use Pay Now on Plan1 with a credit-card payment method and let it succeed.
Expected Output: The Pay Now credit-card payment triggers the Payment Successful letter and its Confirmation Number is the payment number generated for that Pay Now transaction, not for a scheduled installment.
Verification Step: 1. Open Pat1 > Payment Plan > Plan1 and click Pay Now. 2. Choose a payment option, pay with card Card1 and let the transaction succeed. 3. Note the payment number PayNo1 from the resulting receipt. 4. Open the Payment Successful Email generated for this Pay Now payment. 5. Assert the Confirmation Number equals PayNo1. 6. Assert the Amount Paid equals the amount actually collected through Pay Now. 7. Assert only ONE Payment Successful letter is generated for this single Pay Now transaction.

Description: [New] Card Expiry reminder always prints the LAST day of the expiry month as the card expiry date.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with payment plan Plan1 and saved card Card1; Card1 = card stored with an expiry month and year only (no day); Card Expiry reminder enabled for Email and Text in the reminder preference.
Test Data: Card1 saved with an expiry month/year; let the Card Expiry reminder run for Plan1.
Expected Output: Because only month and year are captured for a card, the reminder treats the expiry date as the LAST calendar day of that month and prints that full date in both the Email and the Text version.
Verification Step: 1. Save card Card1 on Plan1 with an expiry month/year. 2. Enable the Card Expiry reminder (Email + Text) for the Payment Plan event type. 3. Let the reminder run for Plan1. 4. Open the generated Email and read the expiry date printed for Card1. 5. Assert the date is the last calendar day of Card1 expiry month in Card1 expiry year. 6. Assert it is not the first day of the month and not a bare month/year string. 7. Open the Text version and assert the identical date is used. 8. Assert the card is identified only by its last 4 digits.

Description: [New] Card Expiry reminder last-day rule is correct for 31-day, 30-day, 28-day and leap-year February expiry months.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1..Pat4 = patients each with a payment plan and a saved card CardA/CardB/CardC/CardD; CardA expires in a 31-day month, CardB in a 30-day month, CardC in a non-leap February, CardD in a leap-year February; Card Expiry reminder enabled.
Test Data: Four cards whose expiry months have 31, 30, 28 and 29 days respectively.
Expected Output: For every card the reminder prints the correct last day of that month: the 31st for a 31-day month, the 30th for a 30-day month, the 28th for a non-leap February and the 29th for a leap-year February.
Verification Step: 1. Set up one plan per card CardA, CardB, CardC and CardD with the expiry months described in the pre-requisite data. 2. Enable the Card Expiry reminder and let it run for all four plans. 3. Open the reminder for CardA and assert the expiry date is the 31st of its month. 4. Open the reminder for CardB and assert the expiry date is the 30th of its month. 5. Open the reminder for CardC and assert the expiry date is the 28th of February. 6. Open the reminder for CardD and assert the expiry date is the 29th of February. 7. Assert no reminder rolls over into the following month. 8. Assert Email and Text versions agree for each card.

Description: [New] A card is not treated as expired before the last day of its expiry month, so scheduled charges before that day still run.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with active payment plan Plan1 and saved card Card1; Card1 expiry month is the current month; Due1 = a scheduled installment date that falls earlier in the same month than the last day.
Test Data: Plan1 with a charge scheduled on Due1, which is before the last day of Card1 expiry month.
Expected Output: The charge on Due1 is attempted normally because Card1 is considered valid until the last day of its expiry month; the card is only treated as expired after that last day.
Verification Step: 1. Open Pat1 > Payment Plan > Plan1 with card Card1 whose expiry month is the current month. 2. Confirm an installment is scheduled on Due1, earlier in the month than its last day. 3. Let the scheduled run execute on Due1. 4. Assert the charge is attempted and not blocked with an expired-card error. 5. Assert the installment status reflects the gateway outcome and is not forced to Overdue purely because of expiry. 6. Assert the Card Expiry reminder for Card1 still quotes the last day of the month as the expiry date. 7. Negative check: confirm no expired-card message is shown for Card1 before that last day.

Description: [New] Every payment-plan notification and reminder e-mail is sent from the clinic e-mail setup address.
Pre-requisite Data: Office1 = clinic with an e-mail setup configured with sender address Sender1; Pat1 = patient of Office1 with payment plan Plan1; notification/reminder preferences enabled for Email for the Payment Plan events (setup, status change, successful, failed, payment due, card expiry).
Test Data: Trigger each payment-plan Email event for Plan1 at Office1.
Expected Output: The From address of every payment-plan notification and reminder Email is Sender1, taken from the clinic e-mail setup — not the logged-in user mailbox and not a hard-coded application address.
Verification Step: 1. Configure Office1 e-mail setup with sender address Sender1. 2. Enable the Email channel for all payment-plan notification and reminder events. 3. Trigger the Payment Plan Setup event by saving Plan1 and open the generated Email. 4. Assert the From/sender address is Sender1. 5. Repeat for the Payment Plan Status Change, Payment Successful, Payment Failed, Payment Due and Card Expiry events. 6. Assert every one of those Emails uses Sender1 as the sender. 7. Negative check: assert none of them is sent from the logged-in user personal mailbox or from a default system address.

Description: [New] Changing the clinic e-mail setup changes the sender of subsequently generated payment-plan e-mails.
Pre-requisite Data: Office1 = clinic with e-mail setup sender Sender1; Sender2 = a different valid sender address; Pat1 = patient of Office1 with payment plan Plan1; at least one payment-plan Email event enabled.
Test Data: Send one payment-plan Email with Sender1, change the clinic e-mail setup to Sender2, then send the same event again.
Expected Output: E-mails generated after the change go out from Sender2; already-sent e-mails keep the sender they were sent with, proving the sender is read from the clinic e-mail setup at send time.
Verification Step: 1. With Office1 e-mail setup = Sender1, trigger a payment-plan Email for Plan1 and note the sender. 2. Assert the sender is Sender1. 3. Change the Office1 e-mail setup sender to Sender2 and save. 4. Trigger the same payment-plan Email event again for Plan1. 5. Assert the new Email is sent from Sender2. 6. Re-open the first Email in the log and assert its recorded sender is still Sender1. 7. Assert no error or blank sender occurs during the change.

Description: [New] Payment-plan e-mails use the e-mail setup of the clinic the plan belongs to when more than one clinic is configured.
Pre-requisite Data: Office1 and Office2 = two clinics with different e-mail setups Sender1 and Sender2; Plan1 = payment plan belonging to Office1; Plan2 = payment plan belonging to Office2; payment-plan Email events enabled for both.
Test Data: Trigger the same payment-plan Email event once for Plan1 and once for Plan2.
Expected Output: The e-mail for Plan1 is sent from Office1 e-mail setup (Sender1) and the e-mail for Plan2 from Office2 e-mail setup (Sender2); the clinic of the plan decides the sender.
Verification Step: 1. Configure different sender addresses Sender1 for Office1 and Sender2 for Office2. 2. Trigger a payment-plan Email event for Plan1 (Office1). 3. Assert the sender is Sender1. 4. Trigger the same event for Plan2 (Office2). 5. Assert the sender is Sender2. 6. Assert the sender does not change when the same user, logged in once, triggers both. 7. Negative check: assert Plan2 e-mail is never sent from Sender1.

Description: [New] A default letter template exists for each of the seven payment-plan events: Payment Successful, Payment Failed, Payment Plan Setup, Payment Plan Status Change, Payment Due, Card Expiry and Payment Plan Agreement.
Pre-requisite Data: A database where the payment-plan default letter templates have been applied; the letter/template setup screen is accessible; Ev1..Ev7 = the seven payment-plan events listed in the description.
Test Data: Open the letter template setup and list the payment-plan templates.
Expected Output: All seven payment-plan default templates are present and usable: Payment Successful, Payment Failed, Payment Plan Setup, Payment Plan Status Change, Payment Due, Card Expiry and the Payment Plan Agreement.
Verification Step: 1. Open the letter/template setup screen and filter to payment-plan templates. 2. Assert a default template exists for Payment Successful. 3. Assert a default template exists for Payment Failed. 4. Assert default templates exist for Payment Plan Setup and Payment Plan Status Change. 5. Assert default templates exist for the Payment Due and Card Expiry reminders. 6. Assert a default Payment Plan Agreement template exists. 7. Assert each of the seven opens without error and has non-empty body content. 8. Negative check: assert none of the seven is missing or shows a blank/placeholder-only body.

Description: [New] The seven payment-plan default templates are applied to all databases by default, without any manual setup.
Pre-requisite Data: DB1 = a database where no one has manually created payment-plan templates; Pat1 = patient in DB1 with payment plan Plan1; notification/reminder preferences for payment-plan events can be enabled in DB1.
Test Data: A fresh database DB1 with no manually created payment-plan letter templates.
Expected Output: Without any manual template creation, all seven payment-plan default templates are already available in DB1 and the notification/reminder events can be enabled and produce fully formatted letters.
Verification Step: 1. Log into DB1 where no payment-plan templates were manually created. 2. Open the letter template setup and assert the seven payment-plan default templates are already present. 3. Enable a payment-plan notification event and assert its default template is auto-selected / available for selection. 4. Trigger that event for Plan1 and open the generated letter. 5. Assert the letter renders with full default content and merged values, not an empty body. 6. Repeat for one reminder event (Payment Due or Card Expiry) and assert the same. 7. Assert the user was never asked to create a template manually.

Description: [New] Each payment-plan default template provides both the Email and the Text layout where the event supports both channels.
Pre-requisite Data: Default payment-plan templates applied to the database; Ev1 = any of Payment Successful, Payment Failed, Payment Plan Setup, Payment Plan Status Change, Payment Due, Card Expiry; both Email and Text channels selectable in the notification/reminder preference.
Test Data: Open each notification/reminder payment-plan template and inspect its Email and Text layouts.
Expected Output: Every payment-plan notification/reminder default template offers both an Email layout and a shorter Text layout, and both can be enabled independently in the preference screen.
Verification Step: 1. Open the letter template setup for the payment-plan notification/reminder events. 2. For each event, assert an Email layout exists with a subject and body. 3. For each event, assert a Text (SMS) layout exists with a short message body. 4. Enable only the Email channel for one event, trigger it and assert only an Email is produced. 5. Enable only the Text channel for the same event, trigger it and assert only a Text is produced. 6. Enable both, trigger it and assert both are produced with consistent values. 7. Assert the Text layout stays short and does not contain the full Email body.

Description: [New] Clicking Agree & Continue on the Agreement sends the agreement to the patient by e-mail when the agreement event is set in the notification preference.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with e-mail Email1 on demographics; Plan1 = saved payment plan for Pat1 whose Agreement window is open; the Agreement event is added and enabled for Email in the notification preference; Office1 = clinic of Plan1 with e-mail setup Sender1.
Test Data: Enable the Agreement event for Email, then click Agree & Continue on Plan1 agreement.
Expected Output: On Agree & Continue the system sends an e-mail to Pat1 at Email1, from Sender1, carrying the payment plan agreement; the plan activation continues as per the client setting.
Verification Step: 1. In the notification preference, enable the Agreement event for the Payment Plan event type with the Email channel. 2. Open Pat1 > Payment Plan, save Plan1 so the Agreement window opens. 3. Click "Agree & Continue". 4. Assert the agreement is recorded as accepted for Plan1. 5. Open the notification/communication log for Pat1 and assert an agreement e-mail was generated at that moment. 6. Assert the e-mail recipient is Email1 and the sender is Sender1. 7. Assert only one agreement e-mail is generated per Agree & Continue click. 8. Negative check: with the Agreement event disabled in the preference, click Agree & Continue on another plan Plan2 and assert no agreement e-mail is generated.

Description: [New] The agreement e-mail carries the agreement document itself, showing the terms the patient accepted.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with e-mail Email1; Plan1 = payment plan with recurring amount Amt1, frequency Freq1 and card Card1 whose Agreement has just been accepted; Agreement event enabled for Email in the notification preference.
Test Data: Accept the agreement on Plan1 and open the resulting e-mail with its agreement document.
Expected Output: The e-mail generated on Agree & Continue includes the agreement document, and that document shows the same plan terms (amount, frequency, payment method, end date) that the patient accepted on screen.
Verification Step: 1. Enable the Agreement event for Email. 2. Open Plan1 agreement and note the Payment Details values shown on screen. 3. Click "Agree & Continue". 4. Open the generated e-mail for Pat1 from the notification log. 5. Assert the agreement document is present in the e-mail (attached or embedded) and can be opened. 6. Assert the document shows the same amount, frequency, payment method and end date noted in step 2. 7. Assert the document shows the agreement acceptance (signature / agreed stamp). 8. Assert the document never shows the full card number, only the masked last 4.

Description: [New] Confirm whether the agreement e-mail must also carry a body text along with the agreement document, and what that body text should say.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with e-mail Email1; Plan1 = payment plan whose agreement has just been accepted; Agreement event enabled for Email in the notification preference.
Test Data: Accept the agreement on Plan1 and inspect the body of the generated e-mail.
Expected Output: Pending confirmation: the source thread asks whether the agreement e-mail should contain a text body plus the agreement document, or only the document, and what the body content should be. No answer was given in the thread, so the expected body content cannot be asserted.
Verification Step: 1. Enable the Agreement event for Email in the notification preference. 2. Open Plan1 agreement and click "Agree & Continue". 3. Open the generated e-mail for Pat1 from the notification log. 4. Record whether the e-mail body contains any text besides the agreement document. 5. If a body text is present, record its exact wording and the merge fields used. 6. Park the result for BA confirmation — do not pass or fail this scenario until the expected body text is confirmed.
Status Comment: Clarification Required - source thread asks whether the agreement e-mail should include a text body along with the agreement document, and what its content should be; no answer given.

Description: [New] The agreement e-mail is only sent when the Agreement event is enabled in the notification preference.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with e-mail Email1; Plan1 and Plan2 = two saved payment plans whose Agreement windows can be opened; the Agreement event can be enabled or disabled in the notification preference.
Test Data: Disable the Agreement event, accept the agreement on Plan1; enable it, accept on Plan2.
Expected Output: With the Agreement event disabled no e-mail is generated on Agree & Continue; with it enabled the agreement e-mail is generated. The plan activation behaviour is unaffected either way.
Verification Step: 1. Disable the Agreement event in the notification preference. 2. Open Plan1 agreement and click "Agree & Continue". 3. Assert the agreement is accepted and Plan1 activates as per the client setting. 4. Assert NO agreement e-mail appears in the notification log for Pat1. 5. Enable the Agreement event for Email. 6. Open Plan2 agreement and click "Agree & Continue". 7. Assert an agreement e-mail is now generated for Pat1. 8. Assert the enabling/disabling of the event never blocks the agreement acceptance itself.

Description: [New] The generated agreement document is stored at the patient level and can be re-opened from the Agreement button.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with payment plan Plan1 whose agreement has been accepted; the patient-level document list / Agreement button on the Payment Plan Info screen is accessible.
Test Data: Accept the agreement on Plan1, then look for the stored document at the patient level.
Expected Output: The agreement document is saved against Pat1 at the patient level and remains viewable through the Agreement button on the Payment Plan Info screen after closing and re-opening the plan.
Verification Step: 1. Open Pat1 > Payment Plan > Plan1 and accept the agreement with "Agree & Continue". 2. Close the plan and navigate away from the patient. 3. Re-open Pat1 and check the patient-level document storage; assert the agreement document is present for Pat1. 4. Open Plan1 again and click the Agreement button. 5. Assert the stored agreement document opens and shows the accepted terms. 6. Assert the stored document is linked to Pat1 and not lost after logout/login. 7. Assert the document is not duplicated for a single acceptance.

Description: [New] Updating the payment plan clears the previous agreement document and a new agreement is shown.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with payment plan Plan1 that already has an accepted agreement document Doc1; Term1 = an editable plan term (for example amount, frequency or end date) that has not yet been locked by a transaction.
Test Data: Change Term1 on Plan1 and save; then inspect the agreement.
Expected Output: On updating the plan the previously stored agreement Doc1 is cleared and a fresh agreement is presented, so the patient can never be left viewing an agreement that no longer matches the plan.
Verification Step: 1. Open Pat1 > Payment Plan > Plan1, which already has accepted agreement document Doc1. 2. Note the terms shown in Doc1. 3. Change Term1 on Plan1 and save the plan. 4. Assert the previous agreement document Doc1 is no longer available as the current agreement for Plan1. 5. Assert a new agreement is presented for acceptance after the save. 6. Click the Agreement button and assert it opens the NEW agreement, not the cleared Doc1. 7. Negative check: assert the old document is not silently retained and shown from the patient level as the current agreement.

Description: [New] The regenerated agreement carries the UPDATED plan terms.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with payment plan Plan1 that has an accepted agreement; Amt1/Freq1/End1 = the original amount, frequency and end date on the agreement; Amt2/Freq2/End2 = the changed values saved on the plan; Plan1 has not yet had its first transaction.
Test Data: Change amount, frequency and end date on Plan1 to Amt2, Freq2, End2 and save; open the regenerated agreement.
Expected Output: The regenerated agreement shows Amt2, Freq2 and End2 — the updated terms — everywhere the old values appeared; no stale value from the cleared agreement remains.
Verification Step: 1. Note the Payment Details values Amt1, Freq1 and End1 on the current agreement of Plan1. 2. Change the plan to Amt2, Freq2 and End2 and save. 3. Open the regenerated agreement. 4. Assert the Payment Amount now shows Amt2. 5. Assert the Payment Frequency now shows Freq2 and the End Date shows End2. 6. Assert the Total Authorized Amount is recalculated from the updated terms. 7. Assert no old value (Amt1, Freq1 or End1) appears anywhere in the regenerated document. 8. Accept the new agreement and assert the stored patient-level document also carries the updated terms.

Description: [New] If the regenerated agreement is skipped after a plan update, it can be re-opened later from the Agreement button with the new terms.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with payment plan Plan1 that previously had an accepted agreement; client setting "Show Agreement on Payment Plan" = Yes but not mandatory; Term1 = an updated plan term saved on Plan1.
Test Data: Update Term1 on Plan1, close the agreement window without agreeing, then re-open it from the Agreement button.
Expected Output: Skipping the regenerated agreement does not bring back the old document; clicking the Agreement button re-opens the new agreement showing the updated terms, ready to be accepted.
Verification Step: 1. Update Term1 on Plan1 and save so the agreement is regenerated. 2. Close the agreement window without clicking "Agree & Continue". 3. Assert the plan is saved and, under the non-mandatory setting, remains active. 4. Click the Agreement button on the Payment Plan Info screen. 5. Assert the agreement that opens shows the UPDATED terms, not the previously accepted ones. 6. Click "Agree & Continue" and assert the new agreement is stored at the patient level. 7. Negative check: before accepting, assert the old cleared agreement is not offered anywhere.

Description: [New] No surcharge line or field appears in any payment-plan notification or reminder letter, because surcharge is deferred to a separate ER.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with payment plan Plan1 and saved card Card1; notification/reminder preferences enabled for the payment-plan Email and Text events; surcharge functionality deferred to a separate ER (fields hidden).
Test Data: Trigger each payment-plan letter for Plan1 and search its content for surcharge wording.
Expected Output: None of the payment-plan letters (Setup, Status Change, Payment Successful, Payment Failed, Payment Due, Card Expiry) shows any surcharge label, surcharge amount or surcharge-inclusive total; amounts shown are the plain plan/installment amounts.
Verification Step: 1. Enable all payment-plan notification and reminder events for Email and Text. 2. Trigger the Payment Plan Setup letter for Plan1 and search the Email and Text for the word "surcharge" — assert it is absent. 3. Repeat for the Payment Plan Status Change letter and assert no surcharge line. 4. Repeat for the Payment Successful letter and assert the Amount Paid is shown without any surcharge breakup line. 5. Repeat for the Payment Failed letter and assert no surcharge amount is quoted. 6. Repeat for the Payment Due and Card Expiry letters and assert no surcharge label appears. 7. Assert no empty surcharge label or zero-value surcharge row is rendered in any of them.

Description: [New] The receipt generated from a payment plan payment shows no surcharge field or column.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with payment plan Plan1 and card Card1; Rec1 = the receipt created by a payment-plan charge or a Pay Now payment on Plan1.
Test Data: Run one payment on Plan1 and open the resulting receipt Rec1 and its print view.
Expected Output: Receipt Rec1 shows only the payment amount with no surcharge field, no surcharge column and no surcharge total, on screen and in the printed copy.
Verification Step: 1. Run a payment on Plan1 (scheduled run or Pay Now) so receipt Rec1 is created. 2. Open Rec1 on screen and inspect every amount field. 3. Assert there is no surcharge field or surcharge column anywhere on the receipt. 4. Assert the receipt total equals the amount actually collected with no surcharge added. 5. Open the print/PDF view of Rec1 and assert no surcharge line is printed. 6. Open the payment row on Transaction Tracking for Rec1 and assert no surcharge column is visible. 7. Negative check: assert no blank or zero surcharge placeholder is displayed.

Description: [New] The Payment Plan Agreement document contains no surcharge clause, field or amount.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with payment plan Plan1 and card Card1; Agreement available for Plan1 per the client setting; surcharge functionality deferred to a separate ER.
Test Data: Open the Agreement preview and the stored agreement document for Plan1 and search for surcharge wording.
Expected Output: The agreement shows the plan amount and total authorized amount without any surcharge line, surcharge clause or surcharge-inclusive total, both in the on-screen preview and in the saved/emailed document.
Verification Step: 1. Open Pat1 > Payment Plan > Plan1 and launch the Agreement preview. 2. Read the Payment Details section and assert no surcharge field is listed. 3. Read Terms & Conditions and assert no surcharge clause is present. 4. Assert the Total Authorized Amount equals the plan amount maths without any surcharge addition. 5. Accept the agreement and open the stored patient-level document. 6. Assert the stored document likewise contains no surcharge wording. 7. Open the agreement e-mail document and assert the same.

Description: [New] The Reconciliation Preference field is visible on the patient payment plan and auto-populates to "No" (Do not reconcile) on a new plan.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with access to the Payment Plan screen; a new (unsaved) payment plan being created for Pat1; no reconciliation preference chosen by the user yet.
Test Data: Click Add to start a new payment plan for Pat1 and read the Reconciliation Preference field.
Expected Output: The Reconciliation Preference field is shown on the payment plan screen and is pre-filled with "No" / Do not reconcile without the user touching it.
Verification Step: 1. Open Pat1 > Payment Plan and click Add to start a new plan. 2. Locate the Reconciliation Preference field on the plan screen. 3. Assert the field is visible and enabled (not hidden behind another tab or section). 4. Assert its value is pre-filled as "No" / Do not reconcile. 5. Save the plan without changing the field. 6. Re-open the saved plan and assert the stored preference is still "No" / Do not reconcile. 7. Negative check: assert the user is never forced to pick a value before saving.

Description: [New] The Reconciliation Preference offers exactly three options: Do not reconcile, Reconcile to self/guarantor only, and Reconcile to family members balance.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient whose client setting "Patient Payment From" is set to Immediate Guarantor / Patient / Dependent Only so the family option is available; Plan1 = a payment plan for Pat1 in edit mode.
Test Data: Open the Reconciliation Preference dropdown on Plan1 and list its options.
Expected Output: The dropdown lists exactly three options — Do not reconcile (default), Reconcile to self / guarantor only, and Reconcile to family members balance — with no extra or obsolete option.
Verification Step: 1. Open Pat1 > Payment Plan > Plan1 in edit mode. 2. Open the Reconciliation Preference dropdown. 3. Assert the option "Do not reconcile" is present and is the default. 4. Assert the option "Reconcile to self / guarantor only" is present. 5. Assert the option "Reconcile to family members balance" is present. 6. Assert the dropdown contains no fourth option. 7. Select each option in turn, save, re-open the plan and assert the selection is retained exactly.

Description: [New] Do not reconcile: the payment creates an Open Credit that is NOT applied to any balance.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with outstanding patient-responsible charges; Plan1 = active payment plan for Pat1 with Reconciliation Preference = Do not reconcile; Amt1 = the installment amount charged; Bal1 = Pat1 outstanding balance before the charge.
Test Data: Run one successful installment of Amt1 on Plan1 while the preference is Do not reconcile.
Expected Output: An Open Credit of Amt1 is created for Pat1 and remains fully unapplied; none of Pat1 outstanding charges is reduced and Bal1 is unchanged.
Verification Step: 1. Note Pat1 outstanding balance Bal1 and the open charges before the run. 2. Confirm Plan1 Reconciliation Preference is "Do not reconcile" and save. 3. Run one successful installment of Amt1 on Plan1. 4. Open the Open Credit list for Pat1 and assert a new Open Credit of Amt1 exists. 5. Assert the Open Credit unapplied amount equals Amt1 (fully unapplied). 6. Assert Pat1 outstanding balance is still Bal1 and no charge shows a new payment applied. 7. Run the Open Credit reconcile event scheduler and assert the Open Credit is STILL unapplied because the preference is Do not reconcile.

Description: [New] Reconcile to self / guarantor only: the Open Credit is applied when the guarantor and the patient are the same person.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient who is their own guarantor (guarantor = patient); Pat1 has patient-responsible charges Chg1 and Chg2 with dates of service DOS1 earlier than DOS2; Plan1 = active payment plan for Pat1 with Reconciliation Preference = Reconcile to self / guarantor only; Amt1 = installment amount, large enough to cover Chg1.
Test Data: Run one successful installment of Amt1 on Plan1 for self-guarantor Pat1, then run the Open Credit reconcile scheduler.
Expected Output: The Open Credit created by the installment is auto-applied to Pat1 own outstanding patient-responsible charges, reducing Pat1 balance by the applied amount.
Verification Step: 1. Confirm Pat1 is their own guarantor and note charges Chg1 (DOS1) and Chg2 (DOS2) with their patient-responsible amounts. 2. Set Plan1 Reconciliation Preference to "Reconcile to self / guarantor only" and save. 3. Run one successful installment of Amt1 on Plan1. 4. Run the Open Credit reconcile event scheduler. 5. Assert the Open Credit is applied to Chg1 first (earliest DOS). 6. Assert Pat1 balance is reduced by the amount applied. 7. Assert only Pat1 own charges were touched and no other person balance changed.

Description: [New] Reconcile to self / guarantor only: nothing is reconciled when the guarantor is a different person from the patient.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient whose guarantor Gua1 is a DIFFERENT person; Pat1 and Gua1 both have outstanding patient-responsible charges; Plan1 = active payment plan for Pat1 with Reconciliation Preference = Reconcile to self / guarantor only; Amt1 = installment amount.
Test Data: Run one successful installment of Amt1 on Plan1 where Gua1 is not the same person as Pat1, then run the reconcile scheduler.
Expected Output: Because the self-only option reconciles only where guarantor and patient are the same, the Open Credit stays unapplied; neither Pat1 nor Gua1 balance is reduced.
Verification Step: 1. Confirm Gua1 is a different person from Pat1 and note both outstanding balances. 2. Set Plan1 Reconciliation Preference to "Reconcile to self / guarantor only" and save. 3. Run one successful installment of Amt1 on Plan1. 4. Run the Open Credit reconcile event scheduler. 5. Assert the created Open Credit is still fully unapplied. 6. Assert Pat1 balance is unchanged. 7. Assert Gua1 balance is unchanged. 8. Negative check: assert no charge of any dependent of Gua1 was touched.

Description: [New] The "Reconcile to family members balance" option is available only when Patient Payment From is set to Immediate Guarantor / Patient / Dependent Only.
Pre-requisite Data: Client setting "Patient Payment From" that can be set to Immediate Guarantor / Patient / Dependent Only or to another value; Pat1 = patient with payment plan Plan1 in edit mode.
Test Data: Set Patient Payment From to Immediate Guarantor / Patient / Dependent Only, open the Reconciliation Preference dropdown on Plan1.
Expected Output: With Patient Payment From set to Immediate Guarantor / Patient / Dependent Only, the family option is offered in the Reconciliation Preference dropdown and can be selected and saved.
Verification Step: 1. Set the client setting "Patient Payment From" to Immediate Guarantor / Patient / Dependent Only. 2. Open Pat1 > Payment Plan > Plan1 in edit mode. 3. Open the Reconciliation Preference dropdown. 4. Assert "Reconcile to family members balance" is listed and selectable. 5. Select it and save the plan. 6. Re-open Plan1 and assert the family option is retained. 7. Assert the other two options remain available alongside it.

Description: [New] The family reconciliation option is not available when Patient Payment From is not set to Immediate Guarantor / Patient / Dependent Only.
Pre-requisite Data: Client setting "Patient Payment From" set to a value OTHER than Immediate Guarantor / Patient / Dependent Only; Pat1 = patient with payment plan Plan1 in edit mode.
Test Data: Set Patient Payment From to a value other than Immediate Guarantor / Patient / Dependent Only and open the Reconciliation Preference dropdown.
Expected Output: The "Reconcile to family members balance" option is not offered (hidden or disabled); only Do not reconcile and Reconcile to self / guarantor only can be chosen.
Verification Step: 1. Set "Patient Payment From" to a value other than Immediate Guarantor / Patient / Dependent Only. 2. Open Pat1 > Payment Plan > Plan1 in edit mode. 3. Open the Reconciliation Preference dropdown. 4. Assert "Reconcile to family members balance" is not selectable (absent or greyed out). 5. Assert "Do not reconcile" and "Reconcile to self / guarantor only" are still available. 6. Save the plan with one of the available options and assert it saves without error. 7. Negative check: assert the family option cannot be forced in by re-opening or refreshing the screen.

Description: [New] Reconcile to family members balance: the Open Credit is applied across the guarantor and the dependents as allowed by the "Allow Payment From" client setting.
Pre-requisite Data: Client setting "Patient Payment From" = Immediate Guarantor / Patient / Dependent Only; client setting parameter "Allow Payment From" = Immediate Family Members; Gua1 = guarantor with dependents Dep1 and Dep2; Pat1 = patient in that family with payment plan Plan1 set to Reconcile to family members balance; each family member has patient-responsible charges with different dates of service; Amt1 = installment amount large enough to cover more than one charge.
Test Data: Run one successful installment of Amt1 on Plan1 in a guarantor/dependent family, then run the reconcile scheduler.
Expected Output: The Open Credit is auto-applied across the guarantor and dependent balances according to the "Allow Payment From: Guarantor Only or Immediate Family Members" setting, reducing the family outstanding balances.
Verification Step: 1. Confirm "Allow Payment From" is set to Immediate Family Members and note the outstanding patient-responsible charges of Gua1, Dep1 and Dep2. 2. Set Plan1 Reconciliation Preference to "Reconcile to family members balance" and save. 3. Run one successful installment of Amt1 on Plan1. 4. Run the Open Credit reconcile event scheduler. 5. Assert the Open Credit is applied to family charges and the applied total does not exceed Amt1. 6. Assert both guarantor and dependent charges are eligible for application (not only the patient own charges). 7. Assert each reduced charge shows the applied amount against the Open Credit. 8. Change "Allow Payment From" to Guarantor Only, repeat with a fresh Open Credit and assert only the guarantor charges are considered.

Description: [New] The user can change the Reconciliation Preference at any time, including in the middle of a running plan.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with an ACTIVE payment plan Plan1 that has already had at least one successful installment; Plan1 Reconciliation Preference currently = Do not reconcile.
Test Data: Open the running plan Plan1 mid-schedule and change the Reconciliation Preference, then save.
Expected Output: The Reconciliation Preference stays editable even after the plan has run; the change saves successfully without being blocked by the post-first-transaction term lock.
Verification Step: 1. Open Pat1 > Payment Plan > Plan1 which already has at least one successful installment. 2. Assert the locked term fields (Plan Code, Amount, Frequency, Start Date) are read-only. 3. Assert the Reconciliation Preference field is still editable. 4. Change the preference to another option and save. 5. Assert the plan saves without any validation error. 6. Re-open Plan1 and assert the new preference is stored. 7. Change it a second time and assert it can be changed again with no limit on the number of changes.

Description: [New] A changed Reconciliation Preference applies to reconciliation performed after the change, not retrospectively to Open Credits already processed.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with outstanding patient-responsible charges and an active payment plan Plan1; Plan1 initially set to Do not reconcile; OC1 = the Open Credit created by an installment run while the preference was Do not reconcile; OC2 = the Open Credit created by the next installment after the preference is changed to a reconcile option.
Test Data: Run one installment with Do not reconcile, change the preference to a reconcile option, then run the next installment.
Expected Output: OC2 (created after the change) is auto-reconciled per the new preference; OC1 remains as it was left when it was processed under the old preference, so the change only drives subsequent reconciliation.
Verification Step: 1. With Plan1 set to Do not reconcile, run one installment and note the created Open Credit OC1 and its unapplied amount. 2. Run the Open Credit reconcile scheduler and assert OC1 stays unapplied. 3. Change Plan1 Reconciliation Preference to a reconcile option and save. 4. Run the next installment so Open Credit OC2 is created. 5. Run the reconcile scheduler again. 6. Assert OC2 is applied to the eligible balances per the new preference. 7. Assert the state of OC1 as previously processed is not retroactively altered by the preference change alone.

Description: [New] Switching the preference from a reconcile option back to Do not reconcile stops further automatic application.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with outstanding patient-responsible charges; Plan1 = active payment plan currently set to a reconcile option and already auto-applying Open Credits; Bal1 = Pat1 outstanding balance at the moment of the switch.
Test Data: Switch Plan1 Reconciliation Preference from a reconcile option back to Do not reconcile, then run the next installment and the scheduler.
Expected Output: After the switch, the Open Credit created by the next installment is left fully unapplied and Pat1 balance stays at Bal1 minus nothing; previously applied amounts are untouched.
Verification Step: 1. Confirm Plan1 is set to a reconcile option and that an earlier installment was auto-applied. 2. Note Pat1 outstanding balance Bal1 and the already-applied Open Credits. 3. Change the Reconciliation Preference to "Do not reconcile" and save. 4. Run the next installment so a new Open Credit is created. 5. Run the Open Credit reconcile event scheduler. 6. Assert the new Open Credit is fully unapplied. 7. Assert Pat1 outstanding balance is unchanged after the scheduler run. 8. Assert the previously applied Open Credits remain applied and are not reversed.

Description: [New] The chosen Reconciliation Preference is stored with the plan and survives reopening, refreshing and re-login.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with saved payment plan Plan1; Opt1 = any Reconciliation Preference option other than the default.
Test Data: Set Plan1 Reconciliation Preference to Opt1, save, then reopen after refresh and re-login.
Expected Output: The stored preference Opt1 is shown every time the plan is opened, and it is the value the reconciliation logic uses.
Verification Step: 1. Open Plan1, set Reconciliation Preference to Opt1 and save. 2. Close and re-open Plan1 and assert the field shows Opt1. 3. Refresh the browser, re-open Plan1 and assert it still shows Opt1. 4. Log out, log back in, re-open Plan1 and assert it still shows Opt1. 5. Open Plan1 from a different entry point (plan level tracking) and assert the same value is shown. 6. Assert the value is not reset to the default "No" on any of these paths.

Description: [New] Auto reconciliation applies the Open Credit to charges by Date of Service, earliest first.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient/guarantor family eligible for reconciliation under the chosen preference; Chg1, Chg2, Chg3 = outstanding patient-responsible charges with dates of service DOS1 < DOS2 < DOS3; Plan1 = payment plan with a reconcile preference; Amt1 = installment amount sufficient to cover Chg1 and Chg2 but not Chg3.
Test Data: Run one installment of Amt1 on Plan1 and run the Open Credit reconcile scheduler with three charges at different dates of service.
Expected Output: The Open Credit is applied first to the charge with the earliest DOS, then to the next earliest, until the credit is exhausted; the latest-DOS charge is left untouched.
Verification Step: 1. Note the outstanding patient-responsible charges Chg1 (DOS1), Chg2 (DOS2) and Chg3 (DOS3) in date-of-service order. 2. Set Plan1 to a reconcile preference and save. 3. Run one installment of Amt1 on Plan1. 4. Run the Open Credit reconcile event scheduler. 5. Assert Chg1 is fully applied first. 6. Assert Chg2 is applied next with whatever credit remains. 7. Assert Chg3 (latest DOS) receives nothing because the credit is exhausted. 8. Assert the sum of all applied amounts equals exactly Amt1 or the credit available, never more.

Description: [New] Auto reconciliation follows pure Date of Service order with NO patient-first or guarantor-first priority.
Pre-requisite Data: Family with guarantor Gua1 and patient Pat1 eligible under the family reconcile preference; charges interleaved by DOS so that the earliest charge belongs to Gua1, the next to Pat1 and the next to Gua1 again; Plan1 = Pat1 payment plan set to reconcile to family members balance; Amt1 = installment amount covering the first two charges only.
Test Data: Create charges whose dates of service alternate between the guarantor and the patient, then run one installment and the reconcile scheduler.
Expected Output: The credit is applied strictly in date-of-service order across the whole eligible group; the patient charges are not served before the guarantor charges (and vice versa) just because of who they belong to.
Verification Step: 1. Note the eligible outstanding charges in date-of-service order and record which person each belongs to (alternating guarantor/patient). 2. Set Plan1 to "Reconcile to family members balance" and save. 3. Run one installment of Amt1 on Plan1. 4. Run the Open Credit reconcile event scheduler. 5. Assert the earliest-DOS charge is applied first even though it belongs to the guarantor and not the patient. 6. Assert the second-earliest charge is applied next regardless of owner. 7. Negative check: assert no later-DOS charge was applied ahead of an earlier-DOS charge because of patient/guarantor priority. 8. Assert the applied sequence, read by DOS, is strictly ascending.

Description: [New] When reconciling a guarantor or dependent balance the system checks that the Date of Service falls inside that person from–to date range.
Pre-requisite Data: Gua1 = guarantor linked to patient Pat1 with an effective from date From1 and to date To1; ChgIn = a patient-responsible charge whose DOS falls inside From1..To1; ChgOut = a charge whose DOS falls outside that range; Plan1 = payment plan set to a reconcile option that covers the guarantor/dependent; Amt1 = installment amount big enough to cover both charges.
Test Data: Run one installment of Amt1 with one in-range charge and one out-of-range charge for the guarantor/dependent, then run the scheduler.
Expected Output: Only ChgIn, whose DOS falls inside the guarantor/dependent from–to range, is reconciled; ChgOut is skipped and the unused credit stays unapplied.
Verification Step: 1. Note the guarantor/dependent link from date From1 and to date To1 for Gua1 and Pat1. 2. Identify ChgIn (DOS inside the range) and ChgOut (DOS outside the range) with their patient-responsible amounts. 3. Set Plan1 to the reconcile option and save. 4. Run one installment of Amt1 and then the Open Credit reconcile event scheduler. 5. Assert ChgIn is applied. 6. Assert ChgOut is NOT applied and still shows its full outstanding amount. 7. Assert the remaining credit stays on the Open Credit as unapplied rather than being forced onto ChgOut. 8. Assert no error is raised while skipping the out-of-range charge.

Description: [New] Charges whose Date of Service falls outside the guarantor/dependent from–to range are skipped and the next eligible charge is taken instead.
Pre-requisite Data: Gua1 = guarantor with link range From1..To1; Chg1 = earliest-DOS charge but OUTSIDE the range; Chg2 = later-DOS charge INSIDE the range; Plan1 = payment plan with a reconcile option covering the guarantor; Amt1 = installment amount covering one charge.
Test Data: Make the earliest-DOS charge fall outside the guarantor link range and the next charge inside it, then run the installment and the scheduler.
Expected Output: The out-of-range earliest charge Chg1 is skipped entirely and the credit moves on to the next eligible in-range charge Chg2, still honouring DOS order among eligible charges.
Verification Step: 1. Note Chg1 (earliest DOS, outside From1..To1) and Chg2 (later DOS, inside the range). 2. Set Plan1 to the reconcile option and save. 3. Run one installment of Amt1 and then the Open Credit reconcile event scheduler. 4. Assert Chg1 is untouched and still fully outstanding. 5. Assert Chg2 is applied instead. 6. Assert the applied amount does not exceed the patient-responsible amount of Chg2. 7. Assert the skip is silent (no failure of the whole reconcile run). 8. Assert re-running the scheduler does not later apply anything to Chg1.

Description: [New] Boundary: a charge whose Date of Service is exactly the guarantor/dependent FROM date is reconciled.
Pre-requisite Data: Gua1 = guarantor/dependent link with from date From1 and to date To1; ChgFrom = a patient-responsible charge whose DOS equals From1 exactly; Plan1 = payment plan with a reconcile option covering that person; Amt1 = installment amount covering ChgFrom.
Test Data: A charge dated exactly on the link from date; run one installment and the reconcile scheduler.
Expected Output: The charge dated exactly on the from date is treated as inside the range and is reconciled — the range check is inclusive of the from date.
Verification Step: 1. Create/identify ChgFrom with DOS exactly equal to From1. 2. Set Plan1 to the reconcile option and save. 3. Run one installment of Amt1 on Plan1. 4. Run the Open Credit reconcile event scheduler. 5. Assert ChgFrom is applied and its outstanding amount is reduced. 6. Assert the Open Credit shows the corresponding applied amount against ChgFrom. 7. Negative check: create a charge dated one day BEFORE From1 and assert it is skipped.

Description: [New] Boundary: a charge whose Date of Service is exactly the guarantor/dependent TO date is reconciled.
Pre-requisite Data: Gua1 = guarantor/dependent link with from date From1 and to date To1; ChgTo = a patient-responsible charge whose DOS equals To1 exactly; Plan1 = payment plan with a reconcile option covering that person; Amt1 = installment amount covering ChgTo.
Test Data: A charge dated exactly on the link to date; run one installment and the reconcile scheduler.
Expected Output: The charge dated exactly on the to date is treated as inside the range and is reconciled — the range check is inclusive of the to date.
Verification Step: 1. Create/identify ChgTo with DOS exactly equal to To1. 2. Set Plan1 to the reconcile option and save. 3. Run one installment of Amt1 on Plan1. 4. Run the Open Credit reconcile event scheduler. 5. Assert ChgTo is applied and its outstanding amount is reduced. 6. Assert the applied amount is recorded against the Open Credit. 7. Negative check: create a charge dated one day AFTER To1 and assert it is skipped and stays fully outstanding.

Description: [New] Only the patient-responsible amount is reconciled by auto reconciliation.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient eligible for reconciliation; ChgMix = an outstanding charge split into a patient-responsible part PR1 and an insurance-pending part INS1; Plan1 = payment plan with a reconcile option; Amt1 = installment amount larger than PR1.
Test Data: A charge carrying both a patient-responsible portion and an insurance-pending portion; run one installment and the scheduler.
Expected Output: The Open Credit is applied only up to the patient-responsible amount PR1 of the charge; the insurance-pending portion INS1 is left untouched and any remaining credit stays unapplied or moves to the next eligible patient-responsible charge.
Verification Step: 1. Note charge ChgMix with its patient-responsible amount PR1 and insurance-pending amount INS1. 2. Set Plan1 to the reconcile option and save. 3. Run one installment of Amt1 on Plan1. 4. Run the Open Credit reconcile event scheduler. 5. Assert the amount applied to ChgMix equals PR1 and no more. 6. Assert the insurance-pending amount INS1 is unchanged on the charge. 7. Assert the leftover credit (Amt1 minus PR1) either moves to the next eligible patient-responsible charge or stays unapplied. 8. Assert the insurance balance total for Pat1 is unchanged.

Description: [New] An amount that is entirely pending with insurance is never reconciled by auto reconciliation.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient eligible for reconciliation; ChgIns = an outstanding charge with the whole amount pending with insurance and zero patient responsibility; Plan1 = payment plan with a reconcile option; Amt1 = installment amount.
Test Data: A charge fully pending with insurance and no other eligible patient-responsible charge; run one installment and the scheduler.
Expected Output: Nothing is applied to the insurance-pending charge; the Open Credit remains fully unapplied and the insurance-pending amount stays exactly as it was.
Verification Step: 1. Confirm ChgIns has zero patient-responsible amount and the full amount pending with insurance. 2. Confirm no other eligible patient-responsible charge exists for the reconciliation scope. 3. Set Plan1 to the reconcile option and save. 4. Run one installment of Amt1 and then the Open Credit reconcile event scheduler. 5. Assert the Open Credit unapplied amount is still Amt1. 6. Assert ChgIns shows no payment applied. 7. Assert the insurance-pending amount on ChgIns is unchanged. 8. Assert no error or stuck scheduler entry results from having nothing to apply.

Description: [New] Auto reconciliation is carried out by the Open Credit reconcile event scheduler.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient eligible for reconciliation with outstanding patient-responsible charges; Plan1 = payment plan with a reconcile option; the Open Credit reconcile event scheduler can be viewed and run; Amt1 = installment amount.
Test Data: Run one installment of Amt1 on Plan1 and observe the Open Credit reconcile event scheduler entry before and after the run.
Expected Output: The installment creates an Open Credit and an entry for the Open Credit reconcile event scheduler; the credit is applied to balances when that scheduler runs, not at the instant of the charge.
Verification Step: 1. Note Pat1 outstanding charges before the run. 2. Set Plan1 to a reconcile option and save. 3. Run one successful installment of Amt1 on Plan1. 4. Immediately check the balances and assert the Open Credit is created and queued for reconciliation. 5. Open the Open Credit reconcile event scheduler and assert an entry exists for this Open Credit. 6. Run the scheduler. 7. Assert the Open Credit is now applied to the eligible charges. 8. Assert the scheduler entry is completed and the same credit is not applied twice on a second run.

Description: [New] If the Open Credit reconcile event scheduler has not run, the Open Credit stays unapplied even when the preference is set to reconcile.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with eligible outstanding patient-responsible charges; Plan1 = payment plan with a reconcile option; the Open Credit reconcile event scheduler is stopped/not yet due; Amt1 = installment amount.
Test Data: Run one installment of Amt1 with the reconcile scheduler not running, then inspect the balances.
Expected Output: The Open Credit exists and is unapplied until the scheduler runs; balances are only changed by the scheduler, never as an untracked side effect of the charge.
Verification Step: 1. Ensure the Open Credit reconcile event scheduler is stopped or not yet due. 2. Set Plan1 to a reconcile option and save. 3. Run one installment of Amt1 on Plan1. 4. Assert the Open Credit is created with the full amount unapplied. 5. Assert Pat1 outstanding charges are unchanged. 6. Start / run the scheduler. 7. Assert the Open Credit is then applied per the preference. 8. Assert nothing was applied before the scheduler ran.

Description: [New] Zero balance: when there is nothing outstanding to reconcile the Open Credit stays fully unapplied.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient (and, for the family option, a family) with a ZERO outstanding patient-responsible balance; Plan1 = payment plan with a reconcile option; Amt1 = installment amount.
Test Data: Run one installment of Amt1 while the eligible balance is zero, then run the reconcile scheduler.
Expected Output: The Open Credit of Amt1 is created and remains fully unapplied because there is no outstanding patient-responsible charge to apply it to; no negative balance is created.
Verification Step: 1. Confirm the eligible outstanding patient-responsible balance for the reconciliation scope is zero. 2. Set Plan1 to a reconcile option and save. 3. Run one successful installment of Amt1 on Plan1. 4. Run the Open Credit reconcile event scheduler. 5. Assert the Open Credit unapplied amount equals Amt1. 6. Assert no charge shows a payment applied. 7. Assert no negative (credit) balance is created on any account. 8. Add a new patient-responsible charge, re-run the scheduler and assert the waiting credit is then applied to it.

Description: [New] Open Credit larger than the total outstanding balance: the leftover amount stays unapplied.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient/family eligible for reconciliation; TotBal1 = the total eligible outstanding patient-responsible balance; Plan1 = payment plan with a reconcile option; Amt1 = installment amount that is GREATER than TotBal1.
Test Data: Run one installment of Amt1 where Amt1 is larger than the total eligible balance TotBal1, then run the scheduler.
Expected Output: All eligible charges are cleared to zero and the leftover (Amt1 minus TotBal1) remains on the Open Credit as an unapplied amount; it is never forced onto ineligible or insurance-pending charges.
Verification Step: 1. Note the total eligible outstanding patient-responsible balance TotBal1 and confirm Amt1 is greater than it. 2. Set Plan1 to a reconcile option and save. 3. Run one installment of Amt1 and then the Open Credit reconcile event scheduler. 4. Assert every eligible charge is reduced to zero outstanding. 5. Assert the Open Credit shows an unapplied amount equal to Amt1 minus TotBal1. 6. Assert no insurance-pending amount was consumed by the leftover. 7. Assert no charge is over-applied (no negative outstanding on any charge). 8. Add a new eligible charge, re-run the scheduler and assert the leftover is then applied to it.

Description: [New] Open Credit smaller than the earliest charge: the earliest-DOS charge is partially applied and the rest stays outstanding.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient eligible for reconciliation; Chg1 = the earliest-DOS eligible charge with a patient-responsible amount LARGER than the installment amount; Plan1 = payment plan with a reconcile option; Amt1 = installment amount smaller than Chg1 patient-responsible amount.
Test Data: Run one installment of Amt1 where Amt1 is smaller than the earliest eligible charge, then run the scheduler.
Expected Output: The whole credit Amt1 is applied to the earliest-DOS charge Chg1, which stays partly outstanding; no later charge receives anything and the Open Credit becomes fully applied.
Verification Step: 1. Note Chg1 as the earliest-DOS eligible charge and confirm its patient-responsible amount exceeds Amt1. 2. Set Plan1 to a reconcile option and save. 3. Run one installment of Amt1 and then the Open Credit reconcile event scheduler. 4. Assert the full Amt1 is applied to Chg1. 5. Assert Chg1 still shows the remaining outstanding difference. 6. Assert no later-DOS charge received any amount. 7. Assert the Open Credit unapplied amount is now zero.

Description: [New] End-to-end: a successful plan charge creates an Open Credit that the scheduler applies to the earliest eligible balances per the chosen preference.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient eligible for reconciliation with several outstanding patient-responsible charges at different dates of service; Plan1 = active payment plan with a reconcile option and card Card1; Amt1 = installment amount; Open Credit reconcile event scheduler available.
Test Data: Run the full cycle on Plan1: charge, Open Credit creation, scheduler run, balance update.
Expected Output: The charge succeeds, an Open Credit of the charge amount is created for Pat1, the reconcile scheduler applies it in DOS order to the eligible patient-responsible balances, and the patient statement/ledger reflects the reduced balances.
Verification Step: 1. Note the outstanding eligible charges of Pat1 in DOS order and the total balance. 2. Confirm Plan1 Reconciliation Preference is a reconcile option. 3. Run a successful installment of Amt1 on Plan1 and confirm the receipt is created. 4. Assert an Open Credit of the collected amount exists for Pat1. 5. Run the Open Credit reconcile event scheduler. 6. Assert the credit is applied in DOS order, earliest first. 7. Assert the total outstanding balance is reduced by exactly the applied amount. 8. Assert the ledger/statement view shows the applications against the correct charges.

Description: [New] Self / guarantor only: dependents balances are never touched even when the patient has nothing outstanding.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient who is their own guarantor with ZERO outstanding patient-responsible balance; Dep1 = a dependent of Pat1 with outstanding patient-responsible charges; Plan1 = Pat1 payment plan set to Reconcile to self / guarantor only; Amt1 = installment amount.
Test Data: Run one installment of Amt1 under the self-only preference with the patient at zero balance and the dependent carrying a balance.
Expected Output: The dependent balance is not reconciled under the self / guarantor only option; the Open Credit stays unapplied even though the dependent owes money.
Verification Step: 1. Confirm Pat1 (self-guarantor) has zero outstanding patient-responsible balance and Dep1 has outstanding charges. 2. Set Plan1 to "Reconcile to self / guarantor only" and save. 3. Run one installment of Amt1 and then the Open Credit reconcile event scheduler. 4. Assert the Open Credit is still fully unapplied. 5. Assert Dep1 outstanding charges are unchanged. 6. Assert no application row is created against any dependent charge. 7. Switch Plan1 to the family option (where allowed), re-run the scheduler and assert the dependent charges then become eligible.

Description: [New] The reconciliation preference does not change how the payment itself is collected or how the receipt is created.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with an active payment plan Plan1 and card Card1; Opt1 and Opt2 = two different Reconciliation Preference options; Amt1 = installment amount.
Test Data: Run one installment with preference Opt1 and one with Opt2 and compare the collection and the receipts.
Expected Output: The amount collected, the receipt created and the installment status are identical for both preferences; only the application of the resulting Open Credit differs.
Verification Step: 1. Set Plan1 to preference Opt1 and run one successful installment of Amt1. 2. Note the collected amount, the receipt and the installment status. 3. Change the preference to Opt2 and run the next installment of Amt1. 4. Assert the collected amount is the same. 5. Assert a receipt is created in both cases with the same structure. 6. Assert the installment status becomes Paid/Success in both cases. 7. Assert the only difference is whether the Open Credit ends up applied to balances. 8. Assert the Payment Successful letter is generated in both cases.

Description: [New] The patient statement shows payment plans associated with the patient or their contact guarantor only.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with payment plan PlanA; Gua1 = the contact guarantor of Pat1 with payment plan PlanB; Other1 = an unrelated patient/guarantor with payment plan PlanC; patient statement can be generated for Pat1.
Test Data: Generate the patient statement for Pat1 while PlanA, PlanB and PlanC exist.
Expected Output: The patient statement for Pat1 lists PlanA (the patient own plan) and PlanB (the contact guarantor plan) only; PlanC of an unrelated party is not shown.
Verification Step: 1. Confirm PlanA belongs to Pat1 and PlanB belongs to the contact guarantor Gua1 of Pat1. 2. Confirm PlanC belongs to an unrelated party Other1. 3. Generate the patient statement for Pat1. 4. Assert PlanA payment plan information is shown. 5. Assert PlanB (contact guarantor plan) information is shown. 6. Assert PlanC is NOT shown anywhere on the statement. 7. Assert the plan details shown (amount, frequency, balance) match the corresponding plan screens.

Description: [New] The patient statement does not show payment plans of a guarantor who is not the patient contact guarantor.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with contact guarantor Gua1; Gua2 = another guarantor in the system who is NOT the contact guarantor of Pat1 and who has payment plan PlanD; patient statement can be generated for Pat1.
Test Data: Generate the patient statement for Pat1 while PlanD exists under a non-contact guarantor Gua2.
Expected Output: PlanD is excluded from the Pat1 patient statement because Gua2 is not the contact guarantor of Pat1.
Verification Step: 1. Confirm Gua1 is the contact guarantor of Pat1 and Gua2 is not. 2. Confirm PlanD belongs to Gua2. 3. Generate the patient statement for Pat1. 4. Assert PlanD does not appear in the payment plan information on the statement. 5. Assert only Pat1 own plans and Gua1 plans appear. 6. Assert the totals on the statement do not include PlanD amounts. 7. Assert the same holds after regenerating the statement.

Description: [New] Guarantor statement with Family Billing OFF shows payment plans associated with the patients and the guarantor.
Pre-requisite Data: Gua1 = guarantor with payment plan PlanG; Pat1 = patient linked to Gua1 with payment plan PlanP; Dep1 = a dependent of Gua1 with payment plan PlanD; Family Billing setting = OFF; guarantor statement can be generated for Gua1.
Test Data: Turn Family Billing OFF and generate the guarantor statement for Gua1.
Expected Output: With Family Billing OFF the guarantor statement lists the plans associated with the guarantor and the directly linked patients (PlanG and PlanP); dependent-only plans are not pulled in.
Verification Step: 1. Set Family Billing to OFF. 2. Confirm PlanG belongs to Gua1, PlanP to the linked patient Pat1 and PlanD to dependent Dep1. 3. Generate the guarantor statement for Gua1. 4. Assert PlanG is listed. 5. Assert PlanP is listed. 6. Assert PlanD (dependent-only) is not listed while Family Billing is OFF. 7. Assert the plan values shown match the plan screens. 8. Assert the statement totals reflect only the listed plans.

Description: [New] Guarantor statement with Family Billing ON shows payment plans associated with the guarantor, the dependents and the patients.
Pre-requisite Data: Gua1 = guarantor with payment plan PlanG; Pat1 = linked patient with payment plan PlanP; Dep1 and Dep2 = dependents of Gua1 with payment plans PlanD1 and PlanD2; Family Billing setting = ON; guarantor statement can be generated for Gua1.
Test Data: Turn Family Billing ON and generate the guarantor statement for Gua1.
Expected Output: With Family Billing ON the guarantor statement lists all plans of the guarantor, the dependents and the linked patients (PlanG, PlanP, PlanD1 and PlanD2).
Verification Step: 1. Set Family Billing to ON. 2. Confirm the plans PlanG, PlanP, PlanD1 and PlanD2 and who they belong to. 3. Generate the guarantor statement for Gua1. 4.
